Since 9.4.0, a Kotlin DSL script that belongs to a build outside the build-tree root is compiled again when the same checkout is at a different path. The usual case is an included build in a sibling directory, such as `pluginManagement { includeBuild("../plugins") }`. #37055 fixed #36964 only for scripts inside the build-tree root.

`KotlinScriptHost.buildTreeScriptPath` makes a script's path relative to the build-tree root when the script is inside it, and keeps the absolute path when it isn't ([v9.8.1](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/v9.8.1/platforms/core-configuration/kotlin-dsl/src/main/kotlin/org/gradle/kotlin/dsl/support/KotlinScriptHost.kt#L61-L72)). That path is an immutable input of the script compilation work in `KotlinScriptEvaluator`. So it changes both the workspace under `caches/<version>/kotlin-dsl/scripts` and the build cache key.

### Expected Behavior

Two checkouts with the same layout at different paths reuse each other's compiled scripts, as they did in 9.3.1.

One way to get there: use `path.relativeTo(buildTreeRootDir)` for scripts outside the root as well. Here that gives `../plugins/settings.gradle.kts`, which is the same in every checkout with this layout.

### Context

Our monorepo has a Gradle build per service, and each one includes shared builds from sibling directories, such as `includeBuild("../tiamat/build-logic")`. Each change is worked on in its own git worktree. Every new worktree therefore compiles the scripts of all those included builds again, and adds new entries to the script cache.

### Self-contained Reproducer Project

The script below creates `checkout-a/app`, which includes `checkout-a/plugins`, and copies it to `checkout-b`. It runs `hello` in each with the same fresh Gradle user home, then prints the scripts each run compiled, read from the build operation trace. Run it as `./repro.sh <path to bin/gradle> <work dir>`.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Usage: repro.sh <gradle launcher> <work dir> [plugins dir relative to app, default ../plugins]
# Creates a root build `app` that includes the build `plugins`, copies it to a
# second path, runs it from each, and prints which scripts each run compiled.
set -euo pipefail

gradle="$1"
work="$2"
plugins="${3:-../plugins}"
rm -rf "$work"
mkdir -p "$work/checkout-a/app" "$work/checkout-a/app/$plugins"

cat > "$work/checkout-a/app/settings.gradle.kts" <<EOF
pluginManagement {
    includeBuild("$plugins")
}
rootProject.name = "app"
EOF
echo 'tasks.register("hello")' > "$work/checkout-a/app/build.gradle.kts"
echo 'rootProject.name = "plugins"' > "$work/checkout-a/app/$plugins/settings.gradle.kts"

cp -R "$work/checkout-a" "$work/checkout-b"

export GRADLE_USER_HOME="$work/gradle-home"

for checkout in checkout-a checkout-b; do
    "$gradle" --no-daemon -q -p "$work/$checkout/app" hello \
        -Dorg.gradle.internal.operations.trace="$work/$checkout-trace"
    echo "== $checkout compiled:"
    python3 - "$work/$checkout-trace-log.txt" <<'EOF'
import json, sys
ops = [json.loads(line) for line in open(sys.argv[1]) if line.startswith('{"displayName"')]
parent = {op["id"]: op.get("parentId") for op in ops}
names = {op["id"]: op["displayName"] for op in ops}
for op in ops:
    if op["displayName"].startswith("Compile script"):
        p = op["id"]
        while p is not None and not names.get(p, "").startswith("Apply "):
            p = parent.get(p)
        print("  ", op["displayName"], "<-", names.get(p))
EOF
    echo "   kotlin-dsl/scripts entries: $(ls "$GRADLE_USER_HOME"/caches/*/kotlin-dsl/scripts | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
done
```

Output with 9.8.1:

```
== checkout-a compiled:
   Compile script settings.gradle.kts (CLASSPATH) <- Apply settings file 'settings.gradle.kts' to settings 'app'
   Compile script settings.gradle.kts (BODY) <- Apply settings file 'settings.gradle.kts' to settings 'app'
   Compile script settings.gradle.kts (CLASSPATH) <- Apply settings file '../plugins/settings.gradle.kts' to settings 'plugins'
   Compile script build.gradle.kts (BODY) <- Apply build file 'build.gradle.kts' to root project 'app'
   kotlin-dsl/scripts entries: 5
== checkout-b compiled:
   Compile script settings.gradle.kts (CLASSPATH) <- Apply settings file '../plugins/settings.gradle.kts' to settings 'plugins'
   kotlin-dsl/scripts entries: 6
```

9.4.1 gives the same result. With 9.3.1, checkout-b compiles nothing.

A third argument of `plugins` puts the included build inside `app/` and includes it with `includeBuild("plugins")`. Then checkout-b compiles nothing on 9.8.1 either.

### Gradle version

9.8.1

### Gradle version that used to work

9.3.1

### Your Environment

macOS 26.6.2 on arm64, Amazon Corretto 25.0.4.

body_text:
### Current Behavior

`ConfigurationCacheProblems` and `KotlinDslPluginEntryCache` implement `java.lang.AutoCloseable`.

https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/v9.8.1/platforms/core-configuration/kotlin-dsl/src/main/kotlin/org/gradle/kotlin/dsl/accessors/KotlinDslPluginEntryCache.kt#L39-L44

https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/v9.8.1/platforms/core-configuration/configuration-cache/src/main/kotlin/org/gradle/internal/cc/impl/problems/ConfigurationCacheProblems.kt#L107-L137

Services are closed by `CompositeStoppable`, but this does not handle `AutoCloseable`.

https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/v9.8.1/platforms/core-runtime/concurrent/src/main/java/org/gradle/internal/concurrent/CompositeStoppable.java#L87-L111

This means the services are not closed after the scope has completed.

Unclosed services causes problems on Windows. `KotlinDslPluginEntryCache` opens file locks, so when the service isn't closed the files aren't released. Windows refuses to delete files opened in other processes. When using TestKit on Windows, JUnit's `@TempDir` sometimes fails to delete the project directory:

```
org.junit.platform.commons.JUnitException: Failed to close extension context
Caused by: java.nio.file.FileSystemException: Failed to delete one or more files. See suppressed exceptions for details.
	Suppressed: java.nio.file.FileSystemException: C:\Users\RUNNER~1\AppData\Local\Temp\Gradle-9-8-1-9.8.1-5065574249326832092\.gradle\9.8.1\kotlin-dsl-plugin-entries\jar-entries.bin: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process
	Suppressed: java.nio.file.FileSystemException: C:\Users\RUNNER~1\AppData\Local\Temp\Gradle-9-8-1-9.8.1-5065574249326832092\.gradle\9.8.1\kotlin-dsl-plugin-entries\kotlin-dsl-plugin-entries.lock: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process
```

Also, the [`DefaultServiceRegistry.close()` Javadoc](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/v9.8.1/platforms/core-runtime/service-registry-impl/src/main/java/org/gradle/internal/service/DefaultServiceRegistry.java#L296-L298) says any service with "a public void close() or stop() method" gets closed, which is not correct. The [class Javadoc](https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/v9.8.1/platforms/core-runtime/service-registry-impl/src/main/java/org/gradle/internal/service/DefaultServiceRegistry.java#L55-L57) is more accurate: only Closeable or Stoppable are handled.



### Expected Behavior

Gradle does not hold file locks after builds have finished.

Gradle services close as expected.

### Current Behavior

when 2 variants have extra unrequested attributes, but 1 has more matched attributes, an ambiguity error occurs. this is only an issue when the variant with more matched attributes has a "peer" variant which contains the same attributes, except some are only compatible, not exact matches (eg java-api and java-runtime) as this case causes the variant we want to not be considered a superset, and therefore the superset rule does not kick in and we drop down to disambiguation

### Expected Behavior

filter out variants lacking a requested attribute when disambiguating

### Context (optional)

Minimal fix is here: https://github.com/gradle/gradle/pull/38883

@jvandort is working on a more comprehensive fix here: https://github.com/gradle/gradle/pull/39435

### Self-contained Reproducer Project

https://github.com/gradle/gradle/pull/38883 has reproducer tests

9.8.1

body_text:
In order for a variety of buildscripts and plugins to function in a user-friendly manner, they set `java.awt.headless=true` in order to prevent macOS from opening a dock icon and stealing focus.

In order to disallow setting system properties under IP (#38708), it's likely best for us to set `java.awt.headless=true` as part of the default daemon configuration, so it's no longer necessary to set this in a plugin at configuration time.

I have found some examples of AWT/Swing being used in buildscripts, but we would allow those to function by passing `-Djava.awt.headless=false` in `org.gradle.jvmargs`.

body_text:
### Expected Behavior

If CC entry is invalidated due to some changed task input, there should be information what inputs changed, at least when running on `--info` level.

Currently, it is hard to diagnose what caused the CC to be invalidated.

If the task in question is at last really re-executed, `--info` tells you at task execution time what was out-of-date.

But if you add to the MCVE from the context below the line `file("foo").writeText("FOO")` on top-level of the build script, then on actual configuration the file is overwritten and thus the task is up-to-date when it comes to executing it and so there is no trace anymore why the CC entry was discarded.

---

Of course it is a bad idea to have such side effects in the configuration phase, but it can happen, and runs fine even with isolated projects.

And this is most probably not a made-up situation.
At least I suspect some setup like that in https://linen.dev/s/gradle-community/t/34624022/why-do-i-get-this-error-message-when-the-task-itself-is-up-t#da4b9ba0-0c81-47a4-9aa5-0d588b77af8d

### Current Behavior (optional)

The build - even on `--info` level - only says
> Calculating task graph as configuration cache cannot be reused because an input to task ':build-logic:jar' has changed.

But there is no trace what did change.

### Context

- Have a build with `build-logic` included build where a plugin of it is applied in the main build.
- In the `build-logic` build script have
   ```kotlin
  tasks.jar {
      from("foo")
  }
  ```
- Have the `foo` file present

- Run some task
- Change the `foo` contents
- Run the task again

### Current Behavior

If `build/test-results/<task>/binary/results-generic.bin` from a previous run is truncated, every later run of the `Test` task fails before running any test:

```
* What went wrong:
Execution failed for task ':test'.
> java.io.EOFException
```

The failure repeats on every run, because the task fails before it rewrites the file. Only deleting the file (or `build/test-results`) gets the build working again.

The read comes from `Test.getPreviousFailedTestClasses()`, which is used to run previously failed classes first. #37886 ("Don't fail the test task if old results file is broken") made this path ignore unreadable files, but only for the header: `hasResultsSafe()` reads the first record, and if that works, `forEachResult` is called and any exception there is rethrown. A file that starts out valid but is cut off further in passes the first check and then fails.

A common way to get such a file is two builds running in the same project directory at the same time (e.g. a test task in an IDE and one in a terminal), which write to the same results file.

### Expected Behavior

An unreadable previous results file is ignored, as the comment in `getPreviousFailedTestClasses()` says ("We ignore if we can't read the old results file, as this is just an optimization"), whether it is broken at the start or further in.

### Context (optional)

We added this to our build as a workaround:

```groovy
tasks.withType(Test).configureEach {
    doFirst {
        new File(binaryResultsDirectory.get().asFile, 'results-generic.bin').delete()
    }
}
```

### Steps to Reproduce

`build.gradle`:

```groovy
plugins { id 'java' }
repositories { mavenCentral() }
dependencies {
    testImplementation 'org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter:6.1.0'
    testRuntimeOnly 'org.junit.platform:junit-platform-launcher:6.1.0'
}
test { useJUnitPlatform() }
```

`src/test/java/Broken.java`:

```java
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
public class Broken { @Test public void broken() { throw new RuntimeException("broken"); } }
```

```bash
./gradlew test                      # fails as expected (test failure)
B=build/test-results/test/binary/results-generic.bin
truncate -s $(( $(stat -c%s $B) / 2 )) $B
rm src/test/java/Broken.java
echo 'import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test; public class Ok { @Test public void ok() {} }' > src/test/java/Ok.java
./gradlew test                      # fails: java.io.EOFException, no tests run
./gradlew test                      # fails again the same way
```

Writing `garbage` over the file instead of truncating it makes the build pass, which is the case covered by the existing integration test.

### Gradle version

9.8.1 (the code is unchanged on `master` at 7cb22acddadd13ae6527d6f16d1762c26a9fbf4e)

### Build scan URL (optional)

_none_

### Your Environment (optional)

Linux, JDK 25

### Current Behavior

Immediately after launching Gradle (9.5.1), it halts with this cryptic message. 

```FAILURE: Build failed with an exception.

* What went wrong:
Gradle could not start your build.
> Could not create service of type BuildLifecycleController using BuildScopeServices.createBuildLifecycleController().
   > Could not create service of type BuildModelController using ConfigurationCacheBuildControllerProvider.createBuildModelController().
      > Could not create service of type OutputFilesRepository using ExecutionBuildServices.createOutputFilesRepository().
         > java.io.IOException: Cannot delete file: c:\nomad\target\gradle-project\buildOutputCleanup\buildOutputCleanup.lock```
```
This is when run using Amazon Corretto Java 25, on a Windows 11 device when the workspace is symlinked. E.g. create a workspace under %USER%/jenkins/workspace/project/name, then create a symlink C:\<name> to point to the workspace. Change working directory to be `C:\<name>\` and execute the gradle build there.

I used Claude to pull down the 9.5.1 source code, and locate the root of the offending stacktrace and create a unit-test for it. You can execute this successfully if you are on a real path, but if you change to a symlinked path, then it will work with Java >= 23, but fail on Java 24 and 25.

[LockProbe.java](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33570646/LockProbe.java)

### Expected Behavior

This should not fail or bomb out.

### Context (optional)

We are trying to build on Jenkins, and depend on that symlink to avoid long path names.

### Self-contained Reproducer Project

I've attached a Lock-Probe.java file, run that

### Gradle version

9.5.1

Already provided as a part of the bug description

body_text:
### Expected Behavior

For every Gradle release `gradle-X-wrapper.jar` should be published into `services.gradle.org/distributions/` alongside the existing `gradle-X-wrapper.jar.sha256` and `gradle-X-wrapper.jar.asc` files.

This does not weaken wrapper validation: the checksum and signature are already published and would be verified exactly as today. It removes the incentive to fetch the jar from incidental sources, such as git tags, that do not match the published checksums.

### Current Behavior (optional)

Currently Gradle release process publishes the `.sha256` and `.asc` for the wrapper jar into `services.gradle.org/distributions/` but not the jar they describe. There is no official, standalone download URL for the wrapper jar of a given version.

Current workarounds:

- **Download from the gradle/gradle git tag.** The tag holds the bootstrap wrapper Gradle builds itself with, not the released one, so it fails checksum verification whenever a release ships a changed wrapper (8.14.6 and 9.8.1, see #39471).
- **Pin a specific gradle/gradle commit** that contains the released jar. This works, but relies on an internal detail of Gradle's repository.
- **Extract it from `gradle-X-bin.zip`**
  (`lib/plugins/gradle-wrapper-main-X.jar` --> `gradle-wrapper.jar`). This is the official artifact, but it means downloading ~130 MB to obtain ~45 KB.

### Context

Related: #39471

The ASF release policy says a source release **should not** contain compiled code (https://www.apache.org/legal/release-policy.html#source-packages). Many ASF projects produce source releases from git tags, so they keep `gradle-wrapper.jar` out of the repository and have `gradlew` download it on first use, verified against a checksum committed in the repository (see also https://github.com/snazy/gradle-wrapper-no-jar).

**Concrete example: Apache Kafka**

Kafka's documented upgrade procedure (https://github.com/apache/kafka/commit/a18384b31112bfb38816402e89b8e7eafd13e402) takes the wrapper checksum from https://gradle.org/release-checksums/ and downloads the jar from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gradle/gradle/v<version>/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar`.

For 9.8.1 these two official sources disagree:
- published 9.8.1 wrapper checksum: `3b8a25775a69158b5ad2b1d17a80a88dc7b40a352a73eb27d06c612a7ce68e98`
- jar at tag `v9.8.1`: `238e777fcddd7e34f9708186085def2abd6e08e658505b38718d79d74c21abd5` (the 9.8.0 wrapper)

As a result, Kafka's `gradlew` fails every other run with "Unable to access jarfile": the downloaded jar never matches the published checksum, so it is deleted on the next run and downloaded again on the one after.

This required a workaround (see Kafka PR below) for what should have been a routine Gradle upgrade (9.7.1 --> 9.8.1) which addresses security advisory GHSA-j5m7-59rp-24f5.

___

Related Kafka PR / Jira ticket:
- Kafka PR: https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23770
- Kafka ticket: https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-21299

body_text:
### Expected Behavior

Version catalogs can hold dependencies whose coordinates don't follow the Maven `group:name:version` shape, so that plugins for other ecosystems can read them from the catalog without workarounds.

For npm, that means being able to declare both scoped and unscoped packages using their real names:

```toml
[versions]
semver = "7.6.0"
actions-cache = "3.0.5"

[libraries]
# https://www.npmjs.com/package/semver
semver        = { name = "semver", version.ref = "semver" } 
# https://www.npmjs.com/package/@actions/cache
actions-cache = { name = "@actions/cache", version.ref = "actions-cache" }
```

Versions declared this way would keep working the same as for Maven libraries: shared `version.ref`s, overrides from `settings.gradle(.kts)`, and published catalogs.


### Current Behavior (optional)

Every catalog library must be a Maven module with a non-empty group and a name:

- `semver = { module = "semver", version.ref = "semver" }` is rejected as invalid syntax.
- `semver = { module = ":semver", version.ref = "semver" }` is also rejected.
- `"@actions/cache"` cannot be written as a name, the scope has to be split out into the group.

Accessors return `MinimalExternalModuleDependency`, which uses a Maven-based `ModuleIdentifier`.

The workaround in use today is to encode the npm scope as the group and invent a placeholder group for unscoped packages, for example `{ module = "npmpkg:semver", ... }`. Every plugin or tool that reads the catalog then has to know that convention and strip the `npmpkg` placeholder.

### Context

Version catalogs are the single place where a build declares its dependency versions, but some Gradle builds also depend on packages from other ecosystems, for example npm packages in Kotlin/JS and Kotlin/WasmJS.

KGP users have requested supporting version catalogs for npm dependencies https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KT-48519.

### Potential solutions

I don't think making `group` optional will help. Npm dependencies should be handled completely differently. One benefit of the version catalog is they are type-safe. Re-using the Maven dependency would allow for invalid usage, like adding a Maven dependency to an `npm()` scope.

```kotlin
kotlin {
  sourceSets {
    webMain {
      dependencies {
        npm(libs.fooJvmLibrary) // should be invalid
        implementation(libs.barNpmPackage) // should be invalid
      }
    }
  }
}
```


One approach would be allowing Gradle settings plugins to register custom entry kinds. KGP could register an 'npm dependency' type which adds a new block into the version catalog.

```
[npm]
is-even = { name = "is-even", version = "1.0.0" }
```

### Current Behavior

When running gradle sync with **resilient sync disabled**, failure does not show the details about broken version catalog file syntax.
IntelliJ 26.3.EAP & Gradle 9.7.1.
Adding empty toml version catalog file with  only `/` in it, running sync.

With resilient sync **enabled** (default behavior now):
```

* What went wrong:

      Location: /Users/mlazeba/IdeaProjects/TomlGradleSimpleProject/gradle/libs.versions.toml line 1
      Possible solution: Fix the TOML file according to the syntax described at https://toml.io.

* Try:
> Run with --scan to get full insights from a Build Scan (powered by Develocity).

CONFIGURE FAILED in 232ms
```

To disable resilient sync need to change flag in IJ registry:
CMD+Shift+A (Search for actions) > Registry > CMD+F (search for) `gradle.use.resilient.model.fetch` > uncheck
Now, with resilient sync **disabled**:
```
FAILURE: Build failed with an exception.

* What went wrong:
org.gradle.api.InvalidUserDataException
> org.gradle.api.InvalidUserDataException

* Try:
> Run with --scan to get full insights from a Build Scan (powered by Develocity).

CONFIGURE FAILED in 5s
```


### Expected Behavior

In both cases error details should be present.

### Context (optional)

We encountered this issue while trying to migrate Android Studio to gradle 9.7.1.
IJ enables resilient sync by default for gradle >= 9.7 but some Android Studio model providers are not ready resulting in other problems with failures reporting.
We tried to disable resilient sync and encountered this.

I asked AI agent to find why this started to happen comparing to gradle 9.6.0, summary below, attaching full report as a file.
[gradle-9-7-toml-sync-error-report.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33727120/gradle-9-7-toml-sync-error-report.md)

#### TL;DR / Root Cause Summary

Even with resilient sync disabled in the IntelliJ registry, this regression is caused by a change in **Gradle 9.7.1** (commit `1ab6b5da384fa31229de16a4f07adbe0461993d1`: *"Propagate resilient model building failures through result types"*) interacting with how `DefaultDependenciesAccessors` wraps TOML errors and how `ContextAwareExceptionHandler` traverses exception chains.

Specifically, **three mechanisms in Gradle combine to swallow the TOML problem details during Sync in 9.7.1**:

1. **`TomlCatalogFileParser.assertNoParseErrors` throws an empty `new InvalidUserDataException()` (`getMessage() == null`)** with the TOML error details attached as `ProblemInternal` objects in `ProblemLocator` rather than in the exception message. Neither `InvalidUserDataException` nor its wrapper is annotated with `@Contextual`.
2. **`DefaultDependenciesAccessors.generateAccessors` catches `Exception` and wraps `InvalidUserDataException` in a raw `new java.lang.RuntimeException(e)`** (`getMessage() == "org.gradle.api.InvalidUserDataException"`), which has no `ProblemInternal` objects attached to it.
3. **In Gradle 9.7.1, `DefaultBuildTreeLifecycleController.fromBuildModel` wraps `beforeTasks` exceptions in `@Contextual BuildActionExecutionException`**. Because `ContextAwareExceptionHandler.visit` only renders `@Contextual` exceptions plus **the direct cause of the last `@Contextual` exception** (`// Show the direct cause of the last contextual cause only`), adding `@Contextual BuildActionExecutionException` at the top causes `ContextAwareExceptionHandler` to stop at its direct cause (`java.lang.RuntimeException`) and **never visit the underlying `InvalidUserDataException` where the TOML `ProblemInternal` details are attached**.



### Self-contained Reproducer Project

- Use IntelliJ 26.3.EAP (or later)
- Create new empty gradle project.
- Ensure Gradle version in wrapper properties is 9.7.1. (any higher probably works as well)
- Create empty toml version catalog file `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, add `/` into it.
- Run Sync to see error. Resilient sync should be enabled now so it should be fine.
- Disable resilient sync: CMD+Shift+A (Search for actions) > Registry > CMD+F (search for) `gradle.use.resilient.model.fetch` > uncheck;
- Run Sync again and see error without details.


### Gradle version

9.7.1

body_text:
### Current Behavior
When an `includeBuild` target is readable but not writable by the user running the build, `./gradlew` exits with status 1 and prints nothing: no `FAILURE` section, no `BUILD FAILED` line, empty stderr, also with `--stacktrace`. The daemon log records the build result as `Success[BuildActionResult]`, and the client calls `exit_group(1)` without writing anything further.

Building the same directory on its own fails with a proper report (`Could not open file hash cache (…/.gradle/9.7.1/fileHashes)` / `Cannot create directory …`), so the failure is presumably the included build's `.gradle` state, but in the composite it never gets reported.

### Expected Behavior
The build fails with the usual failure report naming the directory it can't write.

### Steps to Reproduce
On Linux, as user A, with directory `inc` owned by another user and mode `a+rX,a-w`:

```
# inc/settings.gradle.kts
rootProject.name = "inc"

# app/settings.gradle.kts (owned by A)
rootProject.name = "app"
includeBuild("../inc")
```

body_text:
### Expected Behavior

When a versioned `plugins {}` request fails because the plugin is already on a parent classpath, the error names that classpath and the fix:

```
Plugin 'com.android.application' version '7.1.2' was requested, but the plugin is already
on the classpath of buildSrc, and Gradle cannot tell which version that is.
Remove the version from this request.
```


### Current Behavior (optional)

```
Error resolving plugin [id: 'com.android.application', version: '7.1.2', apply: false]
> The request for this plugin could not be satisfied because the plugin is already on the classpath with an unknown version, so compatibility cannot be checked.
```

The message doesn't say which classpath, or how to fix it.

### Context

The plugin could come from buildSrc, a `buildscript {}` block in settings, the root project or an init script, an included build, or TestKit. Users have to work out which one by trial and error.

A common case is an Android build that puts AGP on the buildSrc classpath for its convention plugins, then uses `alias(libs.plugins.android.application)` in the root build script.

Gradle already has this information. It can walk up the parent class loader scopes to the first one that has the plugin descriptor, and those scopes have names (`buildSrc`, `settings`, `root-project`, `init-script`).

### Related

body_text:
### Expected Behavior

When a versioned `plugins {}` request names a plugin that is already on a parent classpath, Gradle compares the requested version with the version on the classpath. If they match, the request succeeds. If they differ, the build fails with both versions in the message.


### Current Behavior (optional)

Gradle only knows the version of a plugin on a parent classpath if it came from an earlier `plugins {}` block, and only under the exact id that was requested. Otherwise the version is "unknown" and the request fails, even when the versions match.

buildSrc depends on the Kotlin Gradle plugin (KGP) 2.0.21 and the root build requests the same version:

```kotlin
// buildSrc/build.gradle.kts
dependencies {
    implementation("org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-gradle-plugin:2.0.21")
}

// build.gradle.kts
plugins {
    id("org.jetbrains.kotlin.jvm") version "2.0.21" apply false
}
```

This fails with "already on the classpath with an unknown version", although both are 2.0.21. The same happens for `buildscript { dependencies { classpath(...) } }` in settings or the root project.

A second case involves only `plugins {}` blocks. The root project requests `org.jetbrains.kotlin.jvm` version 2.0.21 and a subproject requests `org.jetbrains.kotlin.multiplatform` version 2.0.21. Both ids live in the same jar. Gradle tracked the version of the first id only, so the second request fails as unknown. This was reported in #18786 and closed as a duplicate of #18236, but the version tracking added for #18236 doesn't cover it.


### Context

The module coordinates of buildSrc and `buildscript {}` classpath jars are available at resolution time but are dropped when the classpath becomes a list of files. Keeping them would let Gradle find the jar holding the plugin descriptor and compare its version with the request. For the same-jar case, recording the version for every plugin id in the resolved jar is enough.

body_text:
### Expected Behavior

An aggregating project can lazily select the projects in the build that have a given plugin applied.

```kotlin
configurations.named("aggregateJs") {
  dependencies.addAllLater(
    gradle.projects
      .matching {
        withPlugin("org.jetbrains.kotlin.multiplatform")
      }
      .map { projects -> projects.map { dependencies.project(it.path) } }
  )
}
```

The plugin filter only needs to consider plugins applied in the `plugins {}` block. Dynamically applied plugins can be ignored.

Gradle can read the plugins block without configuring the project, which keeps configure-on-demand working. 

Every selected project is guaranteed to have the expected configurations and attributes. Resolution can stay strict, unselected projects run no tasks, and no settings plugin or custom BuildService is needed.


### Current Behavior (optional)

With Isolated Projects the aggregating project cannot inspect other projects, so there is no good way to find the ones that should be matched.

Listing every project by hand is error prone. New modules must be added in two places, and nothing detects a missing one.

```kotlin
dependencies {
  dokka(project(":a"))
  dokka(project(":b"))
  dokka(project(":c"))
  dokka(project(":d"))
  dokka(project(":f"))
  // oops, missed `:e`!
}
```

Adding a dependency on every project with `allprojects {}` and filtering with a lenient ArtifactView has several problems.

- Gradle treats missing attributes as matches, so projects without the expected plugin can match an unrelated variant.
- Projects that are matched and later filtered out may still run expensive tasks.
- Using `lenient = true` in an ArtifactView hides all resolution errors, not only the expected ones.
- Users can no longer choose the contributing projects themselves.

A shared BuildService where projects register themselves ([example](https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin-wrappers/blob/2035e2311a1a2b03a25f5964f9e435853c8da504/build-logic/wrappersbuild/src/main/kotlin/SubprojectService.kt)) avoids over-matching, but it does not work with configure-on-demand, because unconfigured projects never register.

### Context

### Context

- The Kotlin Gradle Plugin (KGP) collects npm dependencies from every project with a Kotlin JS target and installs them into one shared npm project with one lockfile ([KT-88868](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KT-88868)).
- Dokka aggregates documentation from subprojects. Users currently list every subproject by hand ([Kotlin/dokka#4489](https://github.com/Kotlin/dokka/issues/4489)).
- BOM and publishing projects need every subproject with a certain convention plugin - see [kotlin-wrappers](https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin-wrappers/blob/2035e2311a1a2b03a25f5964f9e435853c8da504/kotlin-wrappers-bom/build.gradle.kts#L7-L13) (#29037).

### Related

- #29037 (since this issue contains a specific proposal I thought a separate issue would be appropriate).
- #25179

{"key": "gradle/gradle#39552", "repository": "gradle/gradle", "issue_number": 39552, "github_issue_id": "5977433118", "url": "https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/39552", "title": "API to fetch projects by applied plugin, compatible with Isolated Projects", "source_files": ["D:\OSS-Mentor\data\teacher_clickhouse\inventory_20261022T172108Z\issues_discovered.json"], "historical_labels": ["a:feature", "to-triage"], "beginner_difficulty_confirmed": false, "frozen": false, "decision": "availability_passed", "reason": "current_unassigned_no_observed_claim_or_open_pr", "open_pr_references": [], "claim_signals": [], "current_labels": ["a:feature", "to-triage"], "current_signal_group": "historical_signal_only", "body": "### Expected Behavior

An aggregating project can lazily select the projects in the build that have a given plugin applied.

```kotlin
configurations.named("aggregateJs") {
  dependencies.addAllLater(
    gradle.projects
      .matching {
        withPlugin("org.jetbrains.kotlin.multiplatform")
      }
      .map { projects -> projects.map { dependencies.project(it.path) } }
  )
}
```

The plugin filter only needs to consider plugins applied in the `plugins {}` block. Dynamically applied plugins can be ignored.

Gradle can read the plugins block without configuring the project, which keeps configure-on-demand working. 

Every selected project is guaranteed to have the expected configurations and attributes. Resolution can stay strict, unselected projects run no tasks, and no settings plugin or custom BuildService is needed.


### Current Behavior (optional)

With Isolated Projects the aggregating project cannot inspect other projects, so there is no good way to find the ones that should be matched.

Listing every project by hand is error prone. New modules must be added in two places, and nothing detects a missing one.

```kotlin
dependencies {
  dokka(project(":a"))
  dokka(project(":b"))
  dokka(project(":c"))
  dokka(project(":d"))
  dokka(project(":f"))
  // oops, missed `:e`!
}
```

Adding a dependency on every project with `allprojects {}` and filtering with a lenient ArtifactView has several problems.

- Gradle treats missing attributes as matches, so projects without the expected plugin can match an unrelated variant.
- Projects that are matched and later filtered out may still run expensive tasks.
- Using `lenient = true` in an ArtifactView hides all resolution errors, not only the expected ones.
- Users can no longer choose the contributing projects themselves.

A shared BuildService where projects register themselves ([example](https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin-wrappers/blob/2035e2311a1a2b03a25f5964f9e435853c8da504/build-logic/wrappersbuild/src/main/kotlin/SubprojectService.kt)) avoids over-matching, but it does not work with configure-on-demand, because unconfigured projects never register.

### Context

### Context

- The Kotlin Gradle Plugin (KGP) collects npm dependencies from every project with a Kotlin JS target and installs them into one shared npm project with one lockfile ([KT-88868](https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KT-88868)).
- Dokka aggregates documentation from subprojects. Users currently list every subproject by hand ([Kotlin/dokka#4489](https://github.com/Kotlin/dokka/issues/4489)).
- BOM and publishing projects need every subproject with a certain convention plugin - see [kotlin-wrappers](https://github.com/JetBrains/kotlin-wrappers/blob/2035e2311a1a2b03a25f5964f9e435853c8da504/kotlin-wrappers-bom/build.gradle.kts#L7-L13) (#29037).

### Related

- #29037 (since this issue contains a specific proposal I thought a separate issue would be appropriate).

The Debug Mode feature allows users to interactively step through their query → transform pipeline by dragging a visual "debug line" to enable/disable queries and transformations. This was completed as part of the hackathon, but the logic, architecture, and overall implementation need refinement.

Debug mode adds an interactive debugging experience to the panel editor:
- Visual Debug Line: A draggable horizontal line in the query/transform list
- Interactive Stepping: Drag the line to enable/disable pipeline steps
- State Preview: See what data looks like at each step of the pipeline
- Toggle Button: Bug icon in the Pipeline header to enter/exit debug mode

### 📁 Implementation files in hackathon branch
- useDebugMode.ts (138 lines) - Custom hook managing debug UI state
- debugModeHelpers.ts (109 lines) - Utilities for state sync/restore
- QueryTransformList.tsx (integration) - Main component with debug line rendering
- PanelDataPane.tsx - State management for debug position

### Current known issues
- State management and state synchronization are **FRAGILE**
- Position calculations need to be refined and hardened
- Needs tests ❗ 

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] State restoration works correctly after reordering items in a non-hacky way
- [ ] Integration tests added and passing
- [ ] Hardcoded dimensions removed or documented
- [ ] Error boundary added
- [ ] Manual testing with 20+ queries/transforms
- [ ] Documentation updated with debug mode usage

## Feature Request

### Use Case

When working with large dashboards that have many panels, users often need to scroll back up to filter/search panels every time they want to adjust criteria. This interrupts the workflow when viewing results in panels further down the dashboard.

This is particularly impactful for panels that control dashboard variables (like search/filter panels), where users frequently need to adjust values while viewing results elsewhere.

### Proposed Solution

Add the ability to pin a panel to a fixed position in the dashboard viewport:

1. **Pin toggle option** in panel settings (similar to how rows can be collapsed)
2. **Fixed positioning** - When pinned, the panel stays visible at the top of the viewport while scrolling
3. **Visual indicator** showing the panel is pinned
4. **Configurable position** - Allow pinning to top, bottom, or side of viewport

### Alternatives Considered

- Duplicating panels at multiple positions (clutters the layout, maintenance overhead)
- Browser extensions to pin elements (not portable across users/browsers)
- Sticky rows (current Grafana feature, but applies to entire rows, not individual panels)

### Context

This feature would significantly improve UX for dashboards with many panels where search/filter criteria need frequent adjustment. It's especially valuable for:
- Operations dashboards with many metrics
- Search panels that control dashboard variables
- Filter panels in complex monitoring setups

### Related

This request originated from a Grafana panel plugin community request: https://github.com/matheus-meneses/grafana-dynamic-search/issues/43

### What happened?

We use the expression `up{job="kubelet",metrics_path="/metrics"}==0` to monitor whether the target is down, but Grafana Alerting applies special handling to the value of 0.

ref:
```

groups:
    - orgId: 1
      name: test
      folder: test
      interval: 10s
      rules:
        - uid: ff98cool4z5s0e
          title: kubelet_Down_10s
          condition: A
          data:
            - refId: A
              relativeTimeRange:
                from: 600
                to: 0
              datasourceUid: xxxxxx
              model:
                editorMode: code
                expr: up{job="kubelet",metrics_path="/metrics"}==0
                instant: true
                intervalMs: 1000
                legendFormat: __auto
                maxDataPoints: 43200
                range: false
                refId: A
          noDataState: OK
          execErrState: Error
          for: 10s
          annotations:
            description: kubelet_Down:{{$labels.node}},instance:{{$labels.instance}}！
            summary: sae{{$labels.sae_cluster}}k8s_kubelet_Down:{{$labels.node}}！
            value: '{{ $values.A.Value }}'
          isPaused: false
          notification_settings:
            receiver: test
```

### What did you expect to happen?

1. value == nil  , NoData
2. *value == [], NoData
3. *value != [], Alerting

### Did this work before?

When *value is zero, Setting Narmal, No Alerting.


https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/844a7332b9032fed016e9aaf7076eebbf2f6460c/pkg/services/ngalert/eval/eval.go#L805-L812

**Why is this needed**:
To display data for generic labels, which may not be numbers.

For example, when displaying usage data of a software by version, I want the version (a short alphanumeric code) to be the x-axis. The ordering is provided by the SQL query based on another field---and Grafana shouldn't care about that.
Please let us use the `Trend` chart for these important use cases 🙏 The new Trend chart is amazing and very polished, it would really be a shame to not be able to use it

**What would you like to be added**:
Just allow users to select non-numerical fields for the x-axis, that's all---no need to add anything.

**Who is this feature for?**
This is will be used by folks in all kinds of domains

### What happened?

Since versions after 11.2.10, Kiosk mode does not hide the variables and time-picker. 

Before:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23911dd6-38fb-4423-b6a8-47b15ee5ccc3


After 11.3:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/859c958f-31fc-4085-82f2-2b23d913a4d2

Most Recentt 12.3:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c2504b3-ec3d-4bf7-b5d1-bf31eec389d0


### What did you expect to happen?

As NOC users, who display grafana dashboards on several screens for network monitoring, It is very important for us to have the most space on our screens dedicated to showing **data**. We pick the variables for the dashboards ONCE, and save the variables as default. Then, on our NOC screens, we want to only see the DATA. No varaibles, no time-picker. 
Version 11.3 and onwards broke this ability. 

The only way to hide it is by appending `&_dash.hideTimePicker=true&_dash.hideVariables=true` but this is impractical and not user-friendly. 

Please at least give us the OPTION in the settings to "Hide Time Picker and Variables in Kios Mode"


### Did this work before?

Yes, as stated, this worked up until version 11.2.10

### How do we reproduce it?

1. Open a dashboard that has variables
2. Click "Enable Kiosk Mode"
3. Variable pickers are not hidden


### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

_No response_

### Environment (with versions)?

Grafana: 11.3 and later
OS: Ubuntu
Browser: Chrome/Firefox


### Grafana platform?

None

### Datasource(s)?

_No response_

body_text: ### What happened? When having a Timeseries graph, using the tooltip to inspect your data shows incorrect data (when using no interpolation) ### Result The _actual_ y value of the snapped measurement is shown in the tooltip (good) The _current_ time position of the cursor is shown in the tooltip (bad) ### What did you expect to happen? The _actual_ time value of the snapped point is shown in the tooltip. ### Did this work before? (much) older timeseries panel did this correct. (eg: grafana 9.2.1) ### Notes Issue was discussued in #36346 too The current behavior could make sense for graphs where you have interpolation. In case your have have graph with just points, I never makes sense to show data where: one of the coordinates is snapped to an actual point, but the other one displaying the position of your cursor. ### How do we reproduce it? 1. Create a timeseries graph, without interpolation. 2. graph has 'sparse' data (to make problem more visible) 3. hover your mouse around a data point ### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel? _No response_ ### Environment (with versions)? Grafana: 12.3.1 OS: any Browser: any ### Grafana platform? A package manager (APT, YUM, BREW, etc.) ### Datasource(s)? _No response_

body_text:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting feature requests -->

**Why is this needed**:

Using the e-mail contact point can quite fast mess up the mailbox. Especially when having multiple alerts and already with only a couple of instances/servers being monitored.


**What would you like to be added**:

tl;dr:
- make the e-mails group in the mail-client so the user can more easily focus on one "storyline" and get a better understanding of the timeline without being distracted by other noise
- this has the additional effect that the alerting e-mails can be collapsed in the mail-client achieving a better overview of all other e-mails
- and last but not least, it allows to integrate with other tools automatically processing the e-mails (I know ideally these tools should be integrated directly via grafana without the detour via e-mail, but sometimes this is just not possible that easy)

Sending alerts via mail I noticed all mails are shown individually. Comparing with other monitoring+alerting solutions one can see some of them create the notifications via mail in a way so that they are shown threaded/grouped. I think this would be very nice to keep track of the alerts triggering and getting resolved.

Digging into this I see this is a feature of most mail-cliets nowadays which is based on (some of) the headers listed under https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5322#section-3.6.4
Basically each mail has an ID set as "Message-ID:" (in my setup, the generated mails have this header already set). Then mails can reference this ID in the "In-Reply-To:" and "References:" headers.

I guess with the flexibility of grafana's alerting the hard challenge is to determine which notifications should be grouped. For this, I'd propose to build upon the "group\_by" setting for a contact point which exists anyhow. As a result we'd get one "thread" per "bucket" where all the alerts are contained with the same values to the keys specified in the "group\_by" setting.

For implementing this, I'm not too familiar with the codebase, but as far as I know at least the alert history is stored somehow. So along with that, we'd need to store the message IDs of the notifications. Then this could be used to craft the two headers I mentioned in line with the RFC regarding

> The `In-Reply-To:` field will contain the contents of the `Message-ID:` field of the message to which this one is a reply (the "parent message"). If there is more than one parent message, then the `In-Reply-To:` field will contain the contents of all of the parents' `Message-ID:` fields.  If there is no `Message-ID:` field in any of the parent messages, then the new message will have no `In- Reply-To:` field.

- search for the last message ID in the group which was triggered

> The `References:` field will contain the contents of the parent's `References:` field (if any) followed by the contents of the parent's `Message-ID:` field (if any). If the parent message does not contain a `References:` field but does have an `In-Reply-To:` field containing a single message identifier, then the `References:` field will contain the contents of the parent's `In-Reply-To:` field followed by the contents of the parent's `Message-ID:` field (if any).  If the parent has none of the `References:`, `In-Reply-To:`, or `Message-ID:` fields, then the new message will have no `References:` field.

- list all message IDs of the group which was triggered
- sort them by name (maybe not needed)
- eliminated duplicates (if we store the message ID along with the alert, multiple alerts might have the same message ID due to the grouping)
- put the IDs into the References header

**Who is this feature for?**

Everyone using grafana for monitoring in combination with an e-mail contact point.

- and last but not least, it allows to integrate with other tools automatically processing the e-mails (I know ideally these tools should be integrated directly via grafana without the detour via e-mail, but sometimes this is just not possible that easy)

Sending alerts via mail I noticed all mails are shown individually. Comparing with other monitoring+alerting solutions one can see some of them create the notifications via mail in a way so that they are shown threaded/grouped. I think this would be very nice to keep track of the alerts triggering and getting resolved.

Digging into this I see this is a feature of most mail-cliets nowadays which is based on (some of) the headers listed under https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5322#section-3.6.4
Basically each mail has an ID set as "Message-ID:" (in my setup, the generated mails have this header already set). Then mails can reference this ID in the "In-Reply-To:" and "References:" headers.

I guess with the flexibility of grafana's alerting the hard challenge is to determine which notifications should be grouped. For this, I'd propose to build upon the "group\_by" setting for a contact point which exists anyhow. As a result we'd get one "thread" per "bucket" where all the alerts are contained with the same values to the keys specified in the "group\_by" setting.

For implementing this, I'm not too familiar with the codebase, but as far as I know at least the alert history is stored somehow. So along with that, we'd need to store the message IDs of the notifications. Then this could be used to craft the two headers I mentioned in line with the RFC regarding

> The `In-Reply-To:` field will contain the contents of the `Message-ID:` field of the message to which this one is a reply (the "parent message"). If there is more than one parent message, then the `In-Reply-To:` field will contain the contents of all of the parents' `Message-ID:` fields.  If there is no `Message-ID:` field in any of the parent messages, then the new message will have no `In- Reply-To:` field.

- search for the last message ID in the group which was triggered

> The `References:` field will contain the contents of the parent's `References:` field (if any) followed by the contents of the parent's `Message-ID:` field (if any). If the parent message does not contain a `References:` field but does have an `In-Reply-To:` field containing a single message identifier, then the `References:` field will contain the contents of the parent's `In-Reply-To:` field followed by the contents of the parent's `Message-ID:` field (if any).  If the parent has none of the `References:`, `In-Reply-To:`, or `Message-ID:` fields, then the new message will have no `References:` field.

- list all message IDs of the group which was triggered
- sort them by name (maybe not needed)
- eliminated duplicates (if we store the message ID along with the alert, multiple alerts might have the same message ID due to the grouping)
- put the IDs into the References header

body_text:
### What happened?

After migration to v12, all my dashboard are extremely slow to load (around 80s)
I use PG as backend database.

I can easily reproduce with a single API call
```
time curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/secure/api/dashboards/uid/cebd10d9-b6e3-49bd-89a0-547a5ad4a1af' -u `cat ~/.grafanapass` -o /dev/null
curl  -u `cat ~/.grafanapass` -o /dev/null 0.00s user 0.00s system 0% cpu 1:18.42 total
```

When looking in logs, I can see this request send on PG database 

```
Jan 29 11:39:10 intreporting grafana[2592266]: logger=sqlstore.xorm t=2026-01-29T11:39:10.674091948+01:00 level=info msg="[SQL] SELECT dashboard.*, dashboard_provisioning.name, dashboard_provisioning.external_id
, dashboard_provisioning.updated as provisioning_updated, dashboard_provisioning.check_sum FROM \"dashboard\" INNER JOIN dashboard_provisioning ON dashboard.id = dashboard_provisioning.dashboard_id WHERE (dashboard_provisioning.dashboard_id = $1) []interface {}{25555} - took: 38.59317ms" caller=[]                                                                                                                            
Jan 29 11:39:10 intreporting grafana[2592266]: logger=sqlstore.xorm t=2026-01-29T11:39:10.675895841+01:00 level=info msg="[SQL] SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM dashboard WHERE org_id=$1 AND is_folder=false []interface {}{7693} - took: 37.370003ms" caller=[]                                                                                                                                                                       
Jan 29 11:39:10 intreporting grafana[2592266]: logger=sqlstore.xorm t=2026-01-29T11:39:10.712765692+01:00 level=info msg="[SQL] SELECT dashboard.*, dashboard_provisioning.name, dashboard_provisioning.external_id
, dashboard_provisioning.updated as provisioning_updated, dashboard_provisioning.check_sum FROM \"dashboard\" INNER JOIN dashboard_provisioning ON dashboard.id = dashboard_provisioning.dashboard_id WHERE (dashboard_provisioning.dashboard_id = $1) []interface {}{25555} - took: 38.435518ms" caller=[]                                                                                                                           
Jan 29 11:39:10 intreporting grafana[2592266]: logger=sqlstore.xorm t=2026-01-29T11:39:10.713822157+01:00 level=info msg="[SQL] SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM dashboard WHERE org_id=$1 AND is_folder=false []interface {}{7694} - took: 37.748885ms" caller=[]
...
```
this query is executed a lot of times
```
grep -c "SELECT dashboard.*, dashboard_provisioning.name, dashboard_provisioning.external_id, dashboard_provisioning.updated as provisioning_updated, dashboard_provisioning.check_sum FROM" postgresql-16-main-2026-01-29_12.log
6030 -- always this count
```

I do not use dashboard provisioning
```
grafana=# SELECT count(*) from dashboard_provisioning;
 count 
-------
     0
```
Some other metrics if it can help
```
grafana=# select count (*) from dashboard;                                                                                                                                                                         
 count 
-------
 12034


grafana=# select count (*) from org;
 count 
-------
  2010
```

I've also tried to add a new empty dashboard and then reload it, same problem. (even in the save action it happens)




### What did you expect to happen?

normal loading time

### Did this work before?

On v11 this was OK
```
time curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/secure/api/dashboards/uid/cebd10d9-b6e3-49bd-89a0-547a5ad4a1af' -u `cat ~/.grafanapass` -o /dev/null
curl -s  -u `cat ~/.grafanapass` -o /dev/null  0.00s user 0.00s system 5% cpu 0.102 total
```

### How do we reproduce it?

1.
2.
3.


### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

_No response_

### Environment (with versions)?

Grafana: 12.1.1
OS: debian 11.11
Browser: N/A


### Grafana platform?

A package manager (APT, YUM, BREW, etc.)

### Datasource(s)?

No

title: Reduce circular dependencies in scenes
warnings_json: ["难度与技能要求为规则推断，尚未经实际构建验证"]

body_text:
Circular dependencies negatively impact our tooling and developer feedback loops. They complicate static analysis and module resolution, making tools slower and less reliable as the codebase grows. In particular, circular imports increase the cost of dependency graph construction, which can significantly affect unit test startup time, test isolation, and watch mode performance. This slows down local development and CI, making iteration and refactoring more expensive over time.

> [!NOTE]  
> Command: yarn dlx madge --circular --extensions ts,tsx public/app/index.ts

title: Reduce circular dependencies in features/dashboard-scene/conditional-rendering
warnings_json: ["难度与技能要求为规则推断，尚未经实际构建验证"]

body_text:
Circular dependencies negatively impact our tooling and developer feedback loops. They complicate static analysis and module resolution, making tools slower and less reliable as the codebase grows. In particular, circular imports increase the cost of dependency graph construction, which can significantly affect unit test startup time, test isolation, and watch mode performance. This slows down local development and CI, making iteration and refactoring more expensive over time.

> [!NOTE]  
> Command: yarn dlx madge --circular --extensions ts,tsx public/app/index.ts

body_text: ### What happened? I know from [this release note][1] that the time comparison feature is available on 12.3. So I installed the __12.3.2 version__ using manual download of the `.tar.xz` file. As written on [this article][2], I tried to enable the feature but encounter this message: Features `timeComparison` and `panelTimeSettings` were not present on the UI: So under the `feature_toggles` section in `grafana.ini` I tried manually enable the feature with: ```ini [feature_toggles] timeComparison = true panelTimeSettings = true ``` I restarted the server but still the __Time Settings__ option won't show on the panel: [1]: https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/whatsnew/whats-new-in-v12-3/ [2]: https://grafana.com/whats-new/2025-10-29-consolidated-panel-time-settings-and-time-comparison/ ### What did you expect to happen? __Time Settings__ should be available like the one shown in [this image](https://grafana.com/media/docs/grafana/panels-visualizations/screenshot-panel-menu-time-settings-v12.3.png?w=750) ### Did this work before? No. It's supposed to be a new feature of 12.3 ### How do we reproduce it? 1. Use Fedora or RHEL base distro 2. Install Grafana 12.3.2 [as a standalone binary](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/setup-grafana/installation/redhat-rhel-fedora/#install-grafana-as-a-standalone-binary) (I don't know if the installation method is relevant) 3. Follow "[Consolidated panel time settings and time comparison](https://grafana.com/whats-new/2025-10-29-consolidated-panel-time-settings-and-time-comparison/)" to enable the feature. ### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel? _No response_ ### Environment (with versions)? Grafana: Grafana OSS v12.3.2 (df2547decd) OS: Fedora Linux 41 (Server Edition) Browser: 144.0.2 ### Grafana platform? A downloaded binary ### Datasource(s)? _No response_

<!-- Please only use this template for submitting feature requests -->

**Why is this needed**:

When creating a link to share for an Explore page with e.g. Prometheus queries, with "Expand results" toggled off, when opening the link "Expand results" is toggled on, altering how the results are displayed.

In my case I'm seeing "Expand results" default to "off" when creating an Explore query, whereas it's defaulting to "on" when opening a generated link to the Explore query.

**What would you like to be added**:

Maintain the same value of the "Expand results" toggle when a share link is created and opened.
Or, default "Expand results" to "off" when a share link is opened.

**Who is this feature for?**

Users sharing and opening Explore page links.

body_text:
We received a couple of customer complaints recently due to some scenarios where undrawably small bucket sizes led to browser crashes or unrendered visualizations. We can catch this case and flag it to users proactively.

The key parts of the code which fail if this happens are:
- https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/f3da78503749b66b931643dc4f38efec83904ae7/public/app/plugins/panel/histogram/Histogram.tsx#L79 can be a divide-by-zero
- https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/f3da78503749b66b931643dc4f38efec83904ae7/packages/grafana-data/src/transformations/transformers/histogram.ts#L203 can be a divide-by-zero, and leads to nonsense buckets
- https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/f3da78503749b66b931643dc4f38efec83904ae7/public/app/plugins/panel/histogram/Histogram.tsx#L50-L62 (this just bugs me - the first method can have an optional index which defaults to 0)

### What happened?

The SqlDatasource.clean() method in @grafana/plugin-ui incorrectly processes SQL-escaped quotes. It converts double single-quotes ('') into a single quote ('). This transformation corrupts valid SQL strings, leading to syntax errors in the database engine because the resulting string literal is unclosed or malformed.

### What did you expect to happen?

SQL-escaped quotes should be preserved exactly as entered. For example, `'a''b'` is a standard SQL representation of the string `a'b` and should remain `'a''b'` after the cleaning process.

### Did this work before?

Yes. This issue does not occur in Grafana's core SQL datasources (such as the PostgreSQL datasource), which correctly handle escaped quotes. The problem seems specific to the SqlDatasource.clean() utility in @grafana/plugin-ui.

### How do we reproduce it?

1. Use a SQL data source plugin that utilizes @grafana/plugin-ui (e.g., DuckDB or similar).
2. Execute the following query:  
```sql
SELECT 'it''s working'
```
3. Observe the query sent to the backend. It is modified to: 
```sql
SELECT 'it's working'
```
4. The database returns a syntax error because the quote after it prematurely closes the string. 
```
error querying the database: Parser Error: syntax error at or near "working" LINE 1: SELECT 'it's working' ^
```

### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

It affects all query entry points, including Dashboard panels and Explore. The issue is rooted in the datasource's shared query processing logic (SqlDatasource.clean()), meaning any query containing escaped quotes will fail regardless of where it is executed.

### Environment (with versions)?

Plugin: motherduckdb/grafana-duckdb-datasource v0.4.0
Grafana: 11.6.0
@grafana/plugin-ui: 0.9.4


### Grafana platform?

Docker

### Datasource(s)?

DuckDB datasource plugin (motherduckdb/grafana-duckdb-datasource) and maybe any other SQL datasource using the shared @grafana/plugin-ui

Add option to use range query to populate dashboard variables from Prometheus data source

**Who is this feature for?**

DevOps whose monitoring targets are expected to be unavailable at times

body_text:
try the following alert setup, it will contain two data source queries and a sql expression:

A:
- testdata datasource, scenario=csv-content
```csv
num, label
15, label1
```

B:
- testdata datasource, scenario=csv-content
```csv
num, label
16, label2
```

C:
- sql expression
```sql
SELECT
  A.num,A.label
FROM
  A
  INNER JOIN B
  ON A.label=B.label
```

the result contains no rows (this is correct), but the alert evaluation will fail with this error message:
```
invalid format of evaluation results for the alert definition C: unexpected field length: 2 instead of 1
```

the problem is that the returned dataframe that represents the "no data" has a shape that is slightly different from what alerting expects.

we return a Frame with two fields, both have zero items in them.

alerting prefers a Frame with no fields at all.
this is also the behavior expected by the dataplane specification: https://grafana.github.io/dataplane/contract/#no-data-and-empty

When configuring an InfluxDB data source in Grafana, the connection test fails if the selected Influx organization contains more than ~20 buckets.
We suspect that Grafana may be using the default limit of 20 in the InfluxDB get_buckets() API call instead of requesting all buckets.


Actual Behavior
Grafana returns the following error:
not found: no buckets found in organization [ORG ID] error reading buckets

The token is valid and has access to exactly one bucket, but Grafana fails to detect it.

### What did you expect to happen?

Grafana should query all buckets in the organization and successfully detect the bucket the token has access to, even if the organization contains more than 20 buckets.

### Did this work before?

I don't know

### How do we reproduce it?

1. Select an influx organization that contains more than 20 buckets (>100 in our case)
2. Create an InfluxDB token with read access to a single bucket.
3. Configure a new InfluxDB data source in Grafana.
4. .Click Save & Test.

### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

_No response_

### Environment (with versions)?

Grafana: 11.6.9
OS: Windows 11
Browser: Microsoft Edge


### Grafana platform?

I don't know

### Datasource(s)?

InfluxDB

body_text:
### What happened?

When provisioning a CloudWatch dashboard via the API (e.g., using Terraform's `grafana_dashboard` resource), if the target JSON omits `metricQueryType` and `metricEditorMode` fields, the Grafana UI renders an empty "Choose" dropdown for "Metric editor mode" and **never fires any CloudWatch query**. Panels silently display "No data" with no error message.

This is particularly confusing because:
1. The same queries work correctly when sent directly to `POST /api/ds/query` — the server-side query runner processes them fine.
2. No error appears in the panel, the browser console, or the network tab — the UI simply never initiates any requests.
3. There is no validation error when saving/importing the dashboard.

### What did you expect to happen?

Either:
- Default `metricQueryType` to `0` (Metric Search) and `metricEditorMode` to `0` (Builder) when these fields are absent, OR
- Display a visible error or warning on the panel indicating the query configuration is incomplete.


### Did this work before?

Haven't tested with prior versions of the plugin

### How do we reproduce it?


1. Create a CloudWatch data source in Grafana 10.4+
2. Import a dashboard with a CloudWatch target that omits `metricQueryType` and `metricEditorMode`:

```json
{
  "targets": [
    {
      "refId": "A",
      "datasource": { "type": "cloudwatch", "uid": "cloudwatch" },
      "namespace": "AWS/Lambda",
      "metricName": "Invocations",
      "dimensions": { "FunctionName": ["my-function"] },
      "statistic": "Sum",
      "period": "60",
      "region": "us-west-2",
      "id": "",
      "expression": "",
      "matchExact": true
    }
  ]
}
```

3. Observe: panel shows "No data", metric editor shows empty "Choose" dropdown.
4. Add `"metricQueryType": 0, "metricEditorMode": 0` to the target — panel immediately works.


### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

Unclear

### Environment (with versions)?

- Grafana version: 10.4 (Amazon Managed Grafana)
- Data source: CloudWatch
- OS: N/A (managed service)
- Browser: Chrome 133

### Grafana platform?

Other

### Datasource(s)?

Cloudwatch

### What happened?

I have a correlation query `{link:traceID="$traceID"}` from Tempo datasource to Tempo datasource, showing me all spans which are linked to my current span. Note: These are not outgoing links (links to other traces) but incoming links (which traces link to the current trace). The trace itself is only a couple milliseconds long. I use the explore tab with Tempo as datasource and the traceid as query. 

When clicking on the correlation link, the following error pops up in the side by side view:
 `Query error
rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = http parameter start must be before end. received start=1771593608 end=1771593608`

Digging through the source code shows that no time shifts are passed to the span (there is no option to configure them anyways).  https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/d3f56b4766f6a32ed367f9853ced3a1af94ba5cc/public/app/features/explore/TraceView/createSpanLink.tsx#L104
Hence, I would expect the correlation to keep the original time range as in the source query. 

### What did you expect to happen?

The correlation time range in the target data source should be the same as the in source datasource, i.e. from now-1h to now. 

### Did this work before?

no

### How do we reproduce it?

1. Configure a tempo to tempo correlation with `{link:traceID="$traceID"}`
2. Go to a trace in the explore tab using tempo
3. Clicking on the correlation for short traces (milliseconds)

### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

no

### Environment (with versions)?

Grafana: 12.3.1
OS: MacOS
Browser: Safari


### Grafana platform?

Kubernetes

### Datasource(s)?

Tempo

<!-- Please only use this template for submitting feature requests -->

**Why is this needed**:

`lokiQuerySplitting` loads partial data before completing. They way it is currently setup, it has `LoadingState.Streaming` until it is done receiving, after which it sets `LoadingState.Done`.

This causes issues, especially with reporting, since streaming data sources are counted as "done" as soon as the stream is setup, hence causing the dashboard and its queries to be considered done too early.

**What would you like to be added**:

Add a `LoadingState.ParitalResult`. It functionally behaves exactly the same as streaming, with the only difference that it is expected to receive a `LoadingState.Done` before being considered done.

**Who is this feature for?**

Data source developers

body_text:
### What happened?

Attempted to log in the usual way with the `Sign in with OAuth` button (which links to the `/login/generic_oauth` endpoint).

The visible response is:
```
Login failed
Failed to get token from provider
```

The server logs show an `invalid_grant`:

`msg="Failed to authenticate request" client=auth.client.generic_oauth error="[auth.oauth.token.exchange] failed to exchange code to token: oauth2: \"invalid_grant\""`

Normally our Grafana instance would call out to `...amazoncognito.com/oauth2/authorize`, then to our Okta, finally returning a valid login session. Instead, in 12.4, Cognito is redirecting back to Grafana instead of Okta.

**To cause this, nothing was changed other than switching to 12.3.4 to 12.4 by changing the Docker image tag from `grafana/grafana:12.3-ubuntu` to `grafana/grafana:12.4-ubuntu`**

I _later_ added the env var `GF_AUTH_GENERIC_OAUTH_VALIDATE_ID_TOKEN` set to `false` and restarted the instance, but that had no useful effect (it should be `false` by default anyway, per the changes made in PR https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/116442 )



### What did you expect to happen?

A successful login

### Did this work before?

This worked as recently as v12.3.4

### How do we reproduce it?

I'm not sure how you'd reproduce it without a Grafana -> Cognito -> Okta flow


### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

No

### Environment (with versions)?

Grafana: 12.4
OS: Ubuntu (whatever version is in `grafana/grafana:12.4-ubuntu`)
Browser: Chrome latest stable


### Grafana platform?

Docker

### Datasource(s)?

n/a

<!-- Please only use this template for submitting feature requests -->

**Why is this needed**:

When a dashboard panel that uses Canvas or browser window is resized (eg: when switching from a large screen to a laptop or resizing the browser), the panel container resizes but the canvas content does not automatically scale or refit.
This causes diagrams like network architecture diagrams to appear clipped or partially hidden unless the user manually zooms out or triggers “Zoom to content”
This makes Canvas panels difficult to use in responsive dashboards, shared links, or environments where screen sizes vary, and requires manual user interaction to restore visibility.

**What would you like to be added**:

An optional Canvas panel setting to automatically fit or scale canvas content when the panel size changes.
Examples:
- Auto “Zoom to content” when the panel is resized
- A toggle such as “Auto-fit canvas on resize”
- A selectable resize behaviour:
- Fit content to panel
- Keep current zoom
- Reset to default zoom

This should be optional and disabled by default to preserve existing Canvas behaviour.


**Who is this feature for?**

This feature is primarily for users building:
- Network topology diagrams
- Infrastructure / architecture diagrams
- Wallboard dashboards
- Dashboards shared across devices with different screen sizes

It would improve usability for viewers (non-editors) and reduce the need for manual zoom interactions when dashboards are resized or viewed on smaller screens.

body_text: ### What happened? My heatmap dashboard panels do not seem to load data correctly when I navigate using the time picker. The missing data shows up when I reload the page. ### What did you expect to happen? When I change the timeframe, the panel should load all available data. ### Did this work before? Been this way since I began placing heatmaps in dashboards, about a year ago. ### How do we reproduce it? * Go to a dashboard that has a heatmap. My heatmap is sourced from a native histogram, not sure if that matters. * Pull up some combination of the filters that is not likely to be cached. * Witness the heatmap show all data. * Now, click `<<` a few times in the dashboard time picker. Eventually you'll see a gap in the data. (I've also seen it when zooming out with the time picker.) * But if you refresh the page one (or sometimes two) times, the gap is gone. ### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel? Internally, I asked for a quick triage, and a dataviz engineer said the problem looked to be in the panel. ### Environment (with versions)? Grafana: OS: Mac Browser: Chrome ### Grafana platform? I use Grafana Cloud ### Datasource(s)? Prometheus (Mimir)

When resizing the Panel Editor, memory usage spikes when the Presets category is open. This seems to come from memory usage to re-render all of the uPlot panels and not from any inherent performance mistakes in the Presets code, so our best course of action would be avoiding the rerenders altogether.

The panel previews scale from about 75 to 100px in width, so maybe if the previews were of a fixed width and didn't scale up and down on resize, the performance would improve. Or maybe we could experiment with a couple of static widths. We should test this theory and see if it looks too janky. Run the update by Antonio to see if there are affordances we could make to avoid this looking bad.

To demonstrate the issue, use the timeseries scenario and set the number of series up to 25, 50, 100, etc.

body_text:
## What happened

`GF_ENVIRONMENT_STACK_ID` and `GF_ENVIRONMENT_STACK_SLUG` environment variables are silently ignored. Setting them has no effect on `cfg.StackID` or `cfg.Slug`.

## Root cause

`applyEnvVariableOverrides()` in `pkg/setting/setting.go` only overrides ini keys that **already exist** in the loaded ini files. Since `defaults.ini` does not define `stack_id` or `stack_slug` in the `[environment]` section, the env vars are never applied.

`cfg.StackID` and `cfg.Slug` are then read from the raw ini section (which has no such keys), so they are always `""`.

## Impact

This breaks the embedded K8s API server namespace mapping — all resources use the `default` namespace (org 1) instead of `stacks-{id}`, and authenticated requests to `stacks-*` namespaces are rejected with "invalid namespace".

## Fix

Use `SectionWithEnvOverrides` (`DynamicSection`) instead of `valueAsString(iniFile.Section(...))` for these two fields. `DynamicSection` checks env vars dynamically for any key, even ones not defined in the ini files. This is the same pattern already used by JWT auth, OAuth, and Zanzana settings.

`GF_ENVIRONMENT_STACK_ID` and `GF_ENVIRONMENT_STACK_SLUG` environment variables are silently ignored. Setting them has no effect on `cfg.StackID` or `cfg.Slug`.

## Root cause

`applyEnvVariableOverrides()` in `pkg/setting/setting.go` only overrides ini keys that **already exist** in the loaded ini files. Since `defaults.ini` does not define `stack_id` or `stack_slug` in the `[environment]` section, the env vars are never applied.

`cfg.StackID` and `cfg.Slug` are then read from the raw ini section (which has no such keys), so they are always `""`.

## Impact

This breaks the embedded K8s API server namespace mapping — all resources use the `default` namespace (org 1) instead of `stacks-{id}`, and authenticated requests to `stacks-*` namespaces are rejected with "invalid namespace".

## Fix

Use `SectionWithEnvOverrides` (`DynamicSection`) instead of `valueAsString(iniFile.Section(...))` for these two fields. `DynamicSection` checks env vars dynamically for any key, even ones not defined in the ini files. **Why is this needed**:

When having metrics where values reach billions, it is very hard to understand how big are the numbers, if one wants to see precise value, like `12345678` looks very similar to `1234567`.

**What would you like to be added**:

Please consider to add thousands delimiter, for example in English `,` is used, which renders number like `12,345,678` or `1,234,567`, but values like that can be easily misinterpreted as `123.456` and `123,456` look similar, but have 3 magnitudes difference.
Ideally, custom separator could be provided, while in Latvian we use `'`, thus values would look like `12'345'678`, `1'234'567` or even `1'234'567.89` 

**Who is this feature for?**

Somebody who has to look at large numbers and still be able to grasp the magnitude of numbers on first look.

**Why is this needed**:

The current Gazetteer [airports.geojson](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/main/public/gazetteer/airports.geojson) was last updated 5 years ago and is missing a number of airports.


**What would you like to be added**:

It might not be feasible to include a list of every single airport in the world due to the expected size of the file, but we should look to refresh this list and at least include all large airports, depending on size extending the medium, small, etc.

Additionally, it would be great if we could somehow automate the process to keep the list updated into the future.

If we do expect the file to be too large, maybe we could simply host the Gazetteers on Github, excluding them from our built releases, but allowing users to reference them in their dashboards (by providing the URL to the Gazetteer field in the panel settings).

[Netrvin/cloudflare-colo-list ](https://github.com/Netrvin/cloudflare-colo-list) is an example of a more complete list - including a process to continuously refresh the data based on Cloudflare locations.

[davidmegginson/ourairports-data](https://github.com/davidmegginson/ourairports-data/blob/main/airports.csv) seems to be a more complete list which is community maintained and updated daily (if there are changes). In this list it mentions types like large/medium/small etc in case we wanted to provide a subset.


**Who is this feature for?**

All Geomap users leveraging the 'Lookup' > 'Gazetteer' > 'Airports' feature

A11y: the current annotation icons do not meet a11y guidelines for folks with vision impairment
Information density: Some users don't want annotations taking up a bunch of space in their panels

**What would you like to be added**:

Allow users to set default annotation size used in panels. Allowing users that desire larger annotations to set larger icon sizes, while others that prefer higher information density can continue to use the small icons.

**Who is this feature for?**

Annotation users
