The cause, at v13.2.3 (the same logic is on `main`):

1. `ConditionalRenderingData._evaluate()` returns `undefined` while the data state is `Loading` or `NotStarted` ([ConditionalRenderingData.tsx#L110-L118](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/6193dc03311b631b9727b560d24369e683dc396e/public/app/features/dashboard-scene/conditional-rendering/conditions/ConditionalRenderingData.tsx#L110-L118)).
2. `ConditionalRenderingGroup.check()` ignores undecided rules and starts from `result = true`, so a group with no decided rule shows its item ([ConditionalRenderingGroup.tsx#L79-L90](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/6193dc03311b631b9727b560d24369e683dc396e/public/app/features/dashboard-scene/conditional-rendering/group/ConditionalRenderingGroup.tsx#L79-L90)).
3. `runRequest` emits a `Loading` packet after 200 ms without a response ([runRequest.ts#L182](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/6193dc03311b631b9727b560d24369e683dc396e/public/app/features/query/state/runRequest.ts#L182)), so each slow refresh puts every data rule back into the undecided state until its response arrives.

I reproduced it on Grafana 13.2.3 with a Prometheus API stub that answers in 600 ms: 3 empty panels showed from page load until their responses, and on each of three refreshes from 200 ms after the click until the responses.

#125353 addressed this together with row-level rules. It kept the last answer during a refresh and rendered an undecided item with `visibility: hidden`. It was closed because evaluating data rules would force query runners to activate, for collapsed rows and for lazy-loaded panels. The refresh case can be fixed on its own inside `ConditionalRenderingData`: remember whether the last completed query had data, and use that while a later query is `Loading`, so no query runner is activated.

First load is harder. #108596 shows a data-ruled panel until its first query completes, because a `display: none` panel has no width and a width-sized query runner does not run. Starting it hidden needs a pending state that keeps the width, as #125353 did with `visibility: hidden`, and that touches the group and the renderers.

### What did you expect to happen?

A panel hidden by a "Has data" rule stays hidden while its query reloads, and only appears once a response with data arrives. Ideally it also starts hidden on first load.

### Did this work before?

No.

### How do we reproduce it?

1. Create a dashboard with an Auto grid layout holding a few stat panels, each with the show/hide rule "Show, Query result: Has data", on a Prometheus query that returns no series.
2. Point them at a data source that takes about 600 ms to answer.
3. Save, exit edit, load the dashboard, then press Refresh a few times.
4. Each panel shows "No data" during the load and from 200 ms into each refresh until its query returns, then disappears.

### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

No.

### Environment (with versions)?

Grafana 13.2.3 (Docker image, also reproduced with the 13.2.3 Linux binary) on Linux, in Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (headless) and desktop Chrome.

### Grafana platform?

Docker

### Datasource(s)?

Not specific to a data source. Seen with Prometheus (Mimir), Loki and a Prometheus API stub.

### What happened?

In Explore, a Tempo `traceql` query (trace ID) disappears when the page is reloaded. Opening the same Explore URL in a new tab also loads Tempo with no query. The trace only shows when Explore opens it in split view, for example from a Loki derived field link.

This breaks Loki -> Tempo derived field links from dashboard Logs panels, because those always open Explore with a fresh page load.

### What did you expect to happen?

Explore restores the Tempo query from the URL and shows the trace, the same as when it opens in split view.

### Did this work before?

Unknown. First noticed on 13.1.4.

### How do we reproduce it?

1. In Explore, run a Loki query that returns logs with `trace_id` as structured metadata. The Loki datasource has a derived field (type: Label, matcher `trace_id`) with an internal link to Tempo, query `${__value.raw}`.
2. Open log details and click the Tempo link. The trace opens in split view and works.
3. Press F5. The trace is gone and the Tempo query is empty.

Also fails:
- Opening the working split-view URL in a new tab
- Clicking the same derived field link from a dashboard Logs panel (v2 dashboard schema)
- Opening a legacy URL directly:
```
  /explore?left={"range":{"from":"now-6h","to":"now"},"datasource":"Tempo","queries":[{"query":"<trace-id>","queryType":"traceql","datasource":{"uid":"Tempo"}}]}
```

Possibly related: #66678

### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

No. It reproduces in Explore alone. Dashboard Logs panels are affected because their links cold-load Explore.

### Environment (with versions)?

Grafana: 13.1.4
Browser: Tested on Google Chrome Version 155.0.8059.40 (Official Build) (arm64) and Opera Neon 136.0.6008.89 (arm64) 
OS: MacOS 26.6.2

### Grafana platform?

I don't know

### Datasource(s)?

Tempo, Loki

# PLG Navigation

## Summary

Grafana's navigation (mega menu in particular) has grown over time with additional sections and plugins being added ad-hoc. This epic/project covers rethinking how users navigate Grafana in a product led growth manner.
We need to think about the information architecture, the design of section-level navigation, how we research and measure it, and the process we use to decide what goes into the nav in the first place.

## Why

- **The nav keeps growing with no defined process for governance.** 
	- On one Cloud stack the frontend nav tree has >100 items across many top-level sections, with the majority coming from plugins. When new items are added, there isn't clear defined process for deciding where it _should_ go 
- **Sections solve the same problems differently.**
	- Dashboards, Alerting, Explore and app plugins each have their own way of handling sub-pages/creation flows (`New {xyz}`)/search/recent or starred items
- **The mega menu does too many jobs.**
	- It is the global switcher, the in-section nav and a creation entry point all at once, and it gets longer every release
- **We lack evidence.**
	- We have opinions about how people navigate, but little shared research or instrumentation to say what's working

## Summary

Grafana's navigation (mega menu in particular) has grown over time with additional sections and plugins being added ad-hoc. This epic/project covers rethinking how users navigate Grafana in a product led growth manner.
We need to think about the information architecture, the design of section-level navigation, how we research and measure it, and the process we use to decide what goes into the nav in the first place.

## Why

- **The nav keeps growing with no defined process for governance.** 
	- On one Cloud stack the frontend nav tree has >100 items across many top-level sections, with the majority coming from plugins. When new items are added, there isn't clear defined process for deciding where it _should_ go 
- **Sections solve the same problems differently.**
	- Dashboards, Alerting, Explore and app plugins each have their own way of handling sub-pages/creation flows (`New {xyz}`)/search/recent or starred items
- **The mega menu does too many jobs.**
	- It is the global switcher, the in-section nav and a creation entry point all at once, and it gets longer every release
- **We lack evidence.**
	- We have opinions about how people navigate, but little shared research or instrumentation to say what's working

- [ ] Avoid breaking changes in grafana/ui plugin bundling when adding new theme tokens (to be done with members of UI Engineering to share knowledge)

**Why is this needed**:

We are deploying Grafana Enterprise as part of our observability suite within a secured DoW cloud hosting environment. To maintain our Authority to Operate (ATO), we have active Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms) in place to address open security findings. 

In Grafana Enterprise 13.0.2 through 13.2.3, the version of the nested dependency github.com/grafana/tempo (v1.5.1-0.20260910130453-bcfe9f230c1d) contains a High-severity vulnerability (CVE-2026-21728). 

Large-limit queries executed in Tempo can trigger massive, uncontrolled memory allocations. Within our shared AKS resource pools, this memory spike can exhaust container resources, trigger Kubernetes Out-Of-Memory (OOM) kills, and disrupt the overall availability of our monitoring services.

**What would you like to be added**:

We request an upgrade of the github.com/grafana/tempo dependency to version 2.8.4, 2.9.2, or 2.10.2 (or higher) to permanently remediate the uncontrolled memory allocation vector. 

If an immediate upgrade is blocked by dependency trees, please implement the following
temporary operational mitigation in the Tempo config:
```
search:
    max_result_limit: 262144
```


**Who is this feature for?**

This enhancement is for the all users, program teams, and mission stakeholders who utilize Grafana for monitoring and must satisfy rigorous ATO compliance standards.

**Who is this feature for?**

This enhancement is for all developers, operators, and program stakeholders leveraging Grafana who require secure data-at-rest encryption and need to achieve or maintain a valid ATO.

**Why is this needed**:

Some self-managed deployments run Grafana inside a service mesh, such as Istio, where a sidecar next to Grafana encrypts traffic. The data source plugin sends traffic to the sidecar without TLS, and the mesh encrypts it between the proxies.

The ClickHouse data source [refuses to connect](https://github.com/grafana/clickhouse-datasource/blob/470e6edc5fb8a161761d6c7b7775dbb3a732050d/pkg/plugin/driver.go#L257-L258) when Forward OAuth Identity is on and the plugin does not set up TLS itself. The error is `JWT authentication requires a secure (TLS) connection`. A community pull request, grafana/clickhouse-datasource#2151, adds a data source setting to turn this check off. Tempo relaxed a similar check for basic auth over gRPC in #123026.

**What would you like to be added**:

A Grafana server setting that states that the network encrypts traffic outside Grafana. A data source that requires its own TLS before it forwards the signed-in user's OAuth identity, such as ClickHouse, can then skip that check. The setting must be off by default. A data source editor must not be able to turn it on alone, because the editor cannot see how the network handles traffic.

**Who is this feature for?**

Teams that run self-managed Grafana in a service mesh, or in another network that encrypts traffic outside the application. These teams use Forward OAuth Identity for per-user access control.

We want to know how many people need this. If you need it, please add a 👍 to this issue. In a comment, name your data source and say which component encrypts the traffic. Do not include hostnames or tokens.

The e2e test `e2e-playwright/test-plugins/grafana-test-panel/tests/useMTPlugins/panelIcons.spec.ts` is marked `test.fixme`. It fails because the canvas icon does not load in the visualization picker.

The cause is a bug in the core meta provider (`apps/plugins/pkg/app/meta/core.go`). The provider returns the meta of the core plugin, also when the plugin has `as_external = true`. Canvas is loaded as external by default in 13.3, so the picker asks for the core logo path, `public/plugins/canvas/img/icn-canvas.svg`. The external canvas plugin does not have this file.

The bug occurs only when `pluginInstallAPISync`, `pluginStoreServiceLoading` and `plugins.useMTPlugins` are on. The e2e tests turn on all three.

Related: https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/134949, https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/134920

As part of https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/133138, we are adding the ability for visualizations to perform basic, ad hoc actions in a way that does not persist to the dashboard settings. This is to enable viewers to tweak what they're looking at to better match with what they may want. 

In https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/134174 this first action was added - showing/hiding columns from the table visualization. Upcoming is https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/134169 which is to allow users to reorder columns in the table visualization.

We would like to keep a registry of the actions that are available on a panel type's configuration. This will serve to be a central place for panel developers to see what actions users will take, so they can account for them in their UI coding. It will also serve to require definitions for future functionality of these actions (for example, we would eventually like people with editor functionality the ability to click and persist a setting to the dashboard, and the mapping between ad hoc action and panel setting may vary. Some settings might persist as a transformation, some as a field override, etc.

The actual logic in these actions is heavily linked with various aspects of that panel's UI, so that will not be kept here.

A very rough prototype of this is demonstrated here https://github.com/grafana/grafana/compare/main...kristina/panel-adhoc-registry . This issue should build this out to something that works for the actions created above after they are merged.

### What happened?

When using Tempo Explore's Breakdown view, an attribute becomes non-selectable as a breakdown dimension once that same attribute is used in the filter bar.

Environment
Grafana: v13.0.1+security-01
Data source: Tempo
View: Explore → Tempo → Metrics → Breakdown

Actual behavior
resource.service.name remains visible in the attribute list.
The attribute receives the filter/funnel indicator.
Clicking resource.service.name does not change the currently selected breakdown attribute.
No error message is displayed.
Other attributes that are not used in filters remain selectable.

The same behavior occurs with other attributes:

namespace
environment
k8s.pod.name
etc.

Once an attribute is used in a filter, it can no longer be selected as the breakdown dimension.

### What did you expect to happen?

The same attribute should be usable both as:

WHERE attribute <condition>

and as the breakdown/group-by dimension.

For example, queries conceptually equivalent to:

WHERE service_name NOT LIKE 'infr.%'
GROUP BY service_name

should be supported.

A common use case is excluding infrastructure services and then breaking down the remaining traffic by service name.

### Did this work before?

Don't know

### How do we reproduce it?

1. Open Traces with Tempo as datasource.
2. Go to Breakdown.
3. Select resource.service.name as the breakdown dimension.
4. Confirm that service breakdown cards are displayed.
5. Add a filter using the same attribute, for example:
   resource.service.name !~ "infr.*"
6. Attempt to select resource.service.name in the Breakdown attribute list again.

### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

_No response_

Grafana:

### Grafana platform?

None

body_text:
## Description

OSS Playwright panel tests are failing in CI for https://github.com/grafana/grafana-enterprise/pull/13870, causing repeated reruns.

Enterprise commit: `61e276c4694c10b4d2005d94db49182edc90cee0`
Workflow: https://github.com/grafana/grafana-enterprise/actions/runs/38717842670

The same five Canvas tests failed in workflow attempts 1 and 2, including their Playwright retries. **Their flakiness is not yet confirmed**; these could be persistent regressions or environment/configuration problems. Separately, Playwright explicitly classified the Table tooltip test as flaky in attempt 2.

### 1. Canvas icon mappings: three failures

File: `e2e-playwright/panels-suite/canvas-icon-mappings.spec.ts`

- Line 7: `should render field-based icons from value mappings correctly`
- Line 25: `should render fixed path icons correctly`
- Line 86: `should display text values from value mappings correctly`

Failure details:
- Text assertions: `getByText('Success')` is not found within 10 seconds.
- Icon assertion: expected at least **5** visible SVG icons; received **0**.

Failed jobs:
- [Attempt 1 — shard 3/8](https://github.com/grafana/grafana-enterprise/actions/runs/38717842670/job/116369702045)
- [Attempt 2 — shard 3/8](https://github.com/grafana/grafana-enterprise/actions/runs/38717842670/job/116379643090)

Both jobs report **3 failed, 94 passed**.

### 2. Canvas scene: two failures

File: `e2e-playwright/panels-suite/canvas-scene.spec.ts`

- Line 20: `should create and render canvas panel with scene elements`
- Line 25: `should handle scene pan and zoom when enabled`

Both fail during setup at line 14:

```text
await panelEditPage.setVisualization('Canvas');

Error: Timeout 15000ms exceeded while waiting on the predicate
```

Failed jobs:
- [Attempt 1 — shard 4/8](https://github.com/grafana/grafana-enterprise/actions/runs/38717842670/job/116369702024)
- [Attempt 2 — shard 4/8](https://github.com/grafana/grafana-enterprise/actions/runs/38717842670/job/116379643267)

### 3. Table nested tooltip: confirmed flaky result

File: `e2e-playwright/panels-suite/table-nested.spec.ts:504`

Test: `Panels test: Table - Nested › tooltip from field`

[Attempt 2 — shard 4/8](https://github.com/grafana/grafana-enterprise/actions/runs/38717842670/job/116379643267) reports this test as **flaky**: it fails initially and passes on retry.

```text
Error: locator.hover: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.
Waiting for locator('[data-testid="data-testid tableng tooltip caret"]').first()

522 | await firstCaret.hover();
```

### Expected outcome

- Investigate and fix the repeated Canvas failures.
- Stabilize the Table tooltip test.
- Determine whether the Canvas failures are specific to Enterprise CI configuration.
- Verify repeated runs pass without relying on retries.

The linked logs include screenshot, error-context, and Playwright trace references. Enterprise job links require repository access.

## Background

`SanitizedSVG` (in `@grafana/ui/unstable` since #135071) strips content from SVGs that do not ship with Grafana:

- `<style>`, `<image>` and `<feImage>` elements
- `style`, `transform` and `overflow` attributes on the outermost `<svg>`

This happens silently. A user whose icon depends on `<style>` classes (common in Illustrator and Inkscape exports) sees it render black or unfilled and has no way to know why.

## Proposal

Add an optional callback that reports what was removed:

```ts
onSanitized?: (report: {
  removed: Array<'style' | 'image' | 'feImage' | 'root-style' | 'root-transform' | 'root-overflow'>;
}) => void;
```

Callers could use it to tell the user that their SVG was changed, for example:

- a panel notice on Canvas and Geomap panels
- a warning in the resource picker preview (URLPickerTab, ResourcePicker, FileUploader)
- a toast

Why it was not added in #135071

The component is unstable, so the prop can go in later without a breaking change. We want to wait for a real consumer before adding it.

Open questions

- Report source: textUtil.sanitizeUntrustedSVGContent returns a string. The report would need a separate function or a different return shape in @grafana/data. That function is already stable, so it cannot change shape.
- Caching: getCleanSVG caches the sanitized string. The report would need to be cached with it, or a cache hit would skip the callback.
- Timing: react-inlinesvg calls preProcessor during load. Decide whether to call onSanitized there or from onLoad.
- Stable promotion: decide whether this needs to land before SanitizedSVG moves to the stable export in 14.

Related

- #135071
- Follow-up: narrow SanitizedSVG props before stable promotion (drop the overridden preProcessor and cacheRequests)
- Docs: the Canvas and Geomap docs do not mention that styles are stripped from external SVGs

Part of #125083
Related issue: #127032
Related PR: #132427

### Problem

`getDataSourceInstance()` from `@grafana/runtime/unstable` is meant to replace `getDataSourceSrv().get()`, but it doesn't behave the same way yet. Because of that, `public/app/plugins/datasource/mixed/MixedDataSource.ts` can't be migrated. In #132427 it emptied Mixed panel data, which **Meticulous** caught, so we reverted it there.

The differences, in `packages/grafana-runtime/src/services/dataSource/dataSource.ts` (`loadDataSourceInstance`) compared with `public/app/features/plugins/datasource_srv.ts` (`loadDatasource`):

- **Plugin meta source:** runtime imports the plugin from `settings.meta`. `get()` resolves `pluginId` with `getPluginIdFromDatasourceInstanceType()`, loads the meta with `getDatasourcePluginMeta(pluginId)`, and only uses `instanceSettings.meta` if that lookup finds nothing.
- **Older plugins that don't extend `DataSourceApi`:** runtime sets `type = settings.type` and `meta = settings.meta`. `get()` sets `type = pluginId` and uses the resolved `meta`.
- **Separate instance cache:** runtime has its own cache (`pluginCache`, keyed by uid). `DatasourceSrv` keeps `this.datasources`, keyed by name/uid. So one datasource can end up with **two live instances**, depending on which API loaded it first.
- **Import failure:** runtime falls back to `get()` only after its own import throws. `get()` then imports the plugin again and caches a second instance. It also shows the `"<name> plugin failed"` alert, which runtime doesn't.

### What needs to happen

- Resolve the plugin meta the same way `get()` does: `getPluginIdFromDatasourceInstanceType()` + `getDatasourcePluginMeta(pluginId)`, falling back to `settings.meta`.
- Patch `type` / `meta` on older plugins the same way `get()` does.
- Share one instance cache between `getDataSourceInstance()` and `DatasourceSrv.get()` (or make one delegate to the other), so a datasource only ever has one instance.
- Make import failures behave the same as `get()`: same error surface, no second import.
- Add parity tests covering these cases, ideally running the same inputs through both APIs.

### Follow-up: migrate `MixedDataSource`

Once the runtime matches `get()`, the Mixed change is small:

- Swap `getDataSourceSrv().get(uid)` for `getDataSourceInstance(uid)`.
- Take the variable's display name (`scopedVars[variable.name].text`) from `api.name` instead of the sync `getDataSourceSrv().getInstanceSettings(uid)` call.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For the same ref, `getDataSourceInstance()` and `getDataSourceSrv().get()` return the **same instance**.
- [ ] Older plugins get the same `type` / `meta` from both paths.
- [ ] A failed plugin import doesn't leave a second cached instance behind.
- [ ] `MixedDataSource.ts` is migrated and Meticulous shows no Mixed panel regressions.

body_text:
**Why is this needed**:

We run Git Sync (Grafana 13.1.0 OSS, pure Git connection to GitLab) with two repositories, both `folderless`, sharing the same directory layout (one directory per project):

- repository A: dashboards edited by teams in the UI (`workflows: [write, branch]`);
- repository B: dashboards generated by CI from Jsonnet, read-only in Grafana (`workflows: []`), since any UI edit would be overwritten by the next render.

Every project that has dashboards in both repositories shows up twice at the root, as two folders with the same title (one marked "Read only"). Users have to look in two places for one project, and folder permissions have to be managed twice.

There is no way around it today:
- A folder is owned by a single repository: if repository B's `_folder.json` uses the UID of a folder created by repository A, the sync fails with `NewFolderManagedByOtherError` ([folders.go#L267](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/v13.1.0/pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/resources/folders.go#L267)).
- A resource's parent folder is always derived from its path in its own repository ([resources.go#L305](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/v13.1.0/pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/resources/resources.go#L305)), so repository B cannot target a folder of repository A.
- Switching repository B to the `folder` target only moves its tree under a wrapper folder: each project is still split in two (`payments` and `B/payments`).
- Merging both into a single repository loses the read-only guarantee, because read-only is a per-repository setting.

**What would you like to be added**:

Let a repository place its resources in a folder owned by another repository, without taking ownership of it. For example, when a directory of repository B has a `_folder.json` whose UID is already managed by repository A, use that folder as the parent instead of failing. Repository A keeps ownership of the folder (title, metadata, deletion); repository B only owns the dashboards it puts inside. Each dashboard keeps the read-only or editable behaviour of its own repository.

Open questions: what happens when repository A deletes a folder that still holds dashboards from repository B (block the deletion, or report it in the sync status); and the behaviour should probably be opt-in, for example a repository setting or an explicit field in `_folder.json`.

An alternative that would also solve our case: read-only paths inside a single repository (for example a glob such as `**/generated-*.json` that the UI refuses to save), so generated and hand-edited dashboards can share one repository and one folder tree.

**Who is this feature for?**

Teams that combine dashboards generated by a pipeline (Jsonnet, Grafonnet, Foundation SDK) with dashboards edited in the UI, and want both organised in the same per-project or per-team folder tree.

- repository B: dashboards generated by CI from Jsonnet, read-only in Grafana (`workflows: []`), since any UI edit would be overwritten by the next render.

Every project that has dashboards in both repositories shows up twice at the root, as two folders with the same title (one marked "Read only"). Users have to look in two places for one project, and folder permissions have to be managed twice.

There is no way around it today:
- A folder is owned by a single repository: if repository B's `_folder.json` uses the UID of a folder created by repository A, the sync fails with `NewFolderManagedByOtherError` ([folders.go#L267](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/v13.1.0/pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/resources/folders.go#L267)).
- A resource's parent folder is always derived from its path in its own repository ([resources.go#L305](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/blob/v13.1.0/pkg/registry/apis/provisioning/resources/resources.go#L305)), so repository B cannot target a folder of repository A.
- Switching repository B to the `folder` target only moves its tree under a wrapper folder: each project is still split in two (`payments` and `B/payments`).
- Merging both into a single repository loses the read-only guarantee, because read-only is a per-repository setting.

**What would you like to be added**:

Let a repository place its resources in a folder owned by another repository, without taking ownership of it. For example, when a directory of repository B has a `_folder.json` whose UID is already managed by repository A, use that folder as the parent instead of failing. Repository A keeps ownership of the folder (title, metadata, deletion); repository B only owns the dashboards it puts inside. Each dashboard keeps the read-only or editable behaviour of its own repository.

Open questions: what happens when repository A deletes a folder that still holds dashboards from repository B (block the deletion, or report it in the sync status); and the behaviour should probably be opt-in, for example a repository setting or an explicit field in `_folder.json`.

An alternative that would also solve our case: read-only paths inside a single repository (for example a glob such as `**/generated-*.json` that the UI refuses to save), so generated and hand-edited dashboards can share one repository and one folder tree.

**Who is this feature for?**

Teams that combine dashboards generated by a pipeline (Jsonnet, Grafonnet, Foundation SDK) with dashboards edited in the UI, and want both organised in the same per-project or per-team folder tree.", ### What happened?

Hi, I found a possible bug with dashboard element references.

Initially, the dashboard contains two tabs with two independent panels:
```
Tab 1 -> Panel A -> panel-1
Tab 2 -> Panel B -> panel-2
```
I then open "Edit as code" and change only the ElementReference in Tab 2 from `panel-2` to `panel-1`

The resulting layout is:
```
Tab 1 -> Panel A -> panel-1
Tab 2 -> Panel A -> panel-1
```
Grafana accepts this dashboard structure, and Panel A initially renders in both tabs.

However, when I edit Panel A from Tab 2, Grafana may navigate to or select Panel A in Tab 1. After changing the panel title and saving the dashboard, the two placements do not update consistently, one placement can show the new title while the other still shows the old title.

I understand that Library Panels are the recommended way to reuse and synchronize panels. I am therefore not sure whether referencing one ordinary dashboard element from multiple layout positions is intended to be supported.

The confusing part is that the v2 schema accepts the duplicate reference and the same element initially renders successfully in both tabs.





### What did you expect to happen?

should either support multiple ref or reject the configuration with a validation error

### Did this work before?

First observed in 13.0.2, reproduced in 13.0.2 and 13.2.2.

### How do we reproduce it?

1. Create a dashboard.
2. Add two tabs: Tab 1 and Tab 2.
3. Add Panel A to Tab 1. It is stored as `panel-1`.
4. Add Panel B to Tab 2. It is stored as `panel-2`.
5. Find the ElementReference for Panel B inside the Tab 2 layout.
6. Change its name from `panel-2` to `panel-1`.
7. Apply the changes.
8. Confirm that Panel A now renders in both tabs.
9. From Tab 2, edit Panel A and change its title.
10. Apply and save the dashboard.
11. Switch between Tab 1 and Tab 2 and compare the panel titles.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa8f63ec-8c0c-4f8d-a4cc-967ebdff7bb6


### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

No

### Environment (with versions)?

Grafana: First observed in 13.0.2, reproduced in 13.0.2 and 13.2.2.
OS: macOS 27.0.1 
Browser: Google Chrome 155.0.8059.80


### Grafana platform?

both K8s / Docker

## Problem

A datasource plugin can have alias IDs. An alias is a legacy plugin ID that a plugin keeps after a rename.

| Alias (legacy ID) | Canonical plugin ID |
| --- | --- |
| `postgres` | `grafana-postgresql-datasource` |
| `phlare` | `grafana-pyroscope-datasource` |
| `testdata` | `grafana-testdata-datasource` |

Grafana still writes aliases to the store, and it still returns them from the new datasource APIs.

- The `data_source` table stores the alias for datasources from before the rename. `postgres` has the highest volume.
- Some write paths still store an alias today. Datasource provisioning stores the `type` from the file without a change. Provisioning runs at each startup, so a file with `type: postgres` writes the alias again each time.
- The unified storage migrator labels each object with the alias group, for example `postgres.datasource.grafana.app`.
- The connections API returns the alias as `plugin`, and it builds `group` from the alias. No server serves that group, because Grafana registers each datasource API group with the canonical ID only.

Effects:

- Clients get API groups that do not exist. The legacy `/api/datasources/uid/:uid` handlers route GET, PUT and DELETE to the group from the connection, so these requests fail for alias rows.
- We expect that unified storage does not list or get migrated alias rows. The list selects on the canonical group label, and the decoder rejects any other label value. We did not confirm this at runtime.
- The frontend works around the alias in `packages/grafana-runtime/src/services/dataSource/sources/mt/mappers.ts`.
- Boot data and the async frontend path can give different `jsonData` for the same datasource. The SQL `database` fallback in `pkg/api/bootdata.go` matches the canonical ID, so `postgres` rows do not get it.

## Why we want to fix this

The new async datasource APIs must return only canonical plugin IDs and canonical API groups. Clients must not need to know about aliases. While Grafana keeps writing aliases, we cannot clean up the stored data, and each client must keep its own alias logic.

## Suggested approach

The approach has three steps.

### 1. Prevent new alias writes

Each write path stores the canonical ID. Use `pluginstore.CanonicalPluginID` (#130100) to resolve the ID.

Known write paths:

- Datasource provisioning. Map the file `type` to the canonical ID, and log a deprecation warning that shows the canonical ID. The provisioning file does not need a change. Correlation provisioning must also use the canonical ID.
- The unified storage migrator. Set the canonical group label.
- Create and update through the per-plugin API. We think that these already store the canonical ID. Add tests to confirm this.
- The legacy `POST /api/datasources` and `PUT /api/datasources`. Check if these store the request `type` without a change.

If the plugin is not installed, Grafana cannot resolve the alias. Then Grafana stores the value without a change, as it does today.

### 2. Map existing records at read time

Records that already contain an alias stay in the store. The read paths map them to the canonical ID:

- The connections API returns the canonical `plugin` and `group`.
- The per-plugin resource gets and lists alias rows, in legacy storage mode and in unified storage mode.
- Unified storage accepts the alias group labels on read, in addition to the canonical label. On write, unified storage sets only the canonical label.
- Boot data matches its per-type tweaks on the canonical ID.

Each time a read maps an alias, Grafana logs it. The log shows the org ID, the datasource UID, the stored alias and the canonical ID. The log must not show `jsonData`, secrets or URLs. These logs tell us when and how often Grafana still reads alias records. If new alias records continue to show up after step 1, a write path is still missing. A counter metric with the alias as its only label can show the same trend. Follow `contribute/backend/instrumentation.md` if we add one.

### 3. Follow-up: migrate stored records

When the logs show that the write paths are fixed, a migration can rewrite the remaining records to the canonical ID. Decide the scope later. Possible parts:

- The `type` column in the `data_source` table.
- The group labels of objects in unified storage.
- Datasource references in dashboards and queries that use an alias.

The provisioning fix from step 1 must ship before the migration. If it does not, provisioning writes the alias back at the next startup.

After the backend changes ship, the frontend can remove its alias workarounds or keep them only as a fallback for older backends.

## Order of work

- Make unified storage and the per-plugin resource serve alias rows before the connections API returns canonical groups. If the order is different, the legacy `/api/datasources/uid/:uid` handlers route to a group that cannot serve the row.
- Ship the boot data tweak fix no later than the connections change, so that boot data and the async path stay at parity.
- Keep frontend changes and backend changes in separate PRs.

## Open questions

1. **Datasources without an installed plugin.** Should the connections API omit them from the list, or return them with a flag? If the API also omits them on get by UID, the legacy DELETE returns 404, and users cannot remove these datasources.
2. **Deploy order.** Unified storage can deploy at a different time than the API layer. The read change and the label change must work in both deploy orders. Check that the oldest storage server that we support handles the `in` label selector on all list paths. Refer to `pkg/storage/unified/AGENTS.md`.
3. **Log volume.** A log line on each mapped read can be noisy. Decide the log level, and decide if we need a rate limit.

{"key": "grafana/grafana#135314", "repository": "grafana/grafana", "issue_number": 135314, "github_issue_id": "5923830526", "url": "https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/135314", "title": "Datasource APIs: Return only canonical plugin IDs and API groups", "source_files": ["D:\OSS-Mentor\data\teacher_clickhouse\inventory_20261022T172108Z\issues_discovered.json"], "historical_labels": ["internal"], "beginner_difficulty_confirmed": false, "frozen": false, "decision": "availability_passed", "reason": "current_unassigned_no_observed_claim_or_open_pr", "open_pr_references": [], "claim_signals": [], "current_labels": ["internal"], "current_signal_group": "historical_signal_only", "body": "## Summary

A datasource plugin can have alias IDs. An alias is an old plugin ID that a rename keeps.
The `data_source` table still stores the old ID for datasources from before the rename.

The new async datasource APIs must return only the canonical plugin ID and the canonical API group.
Clients must not need to resolve aliases.

Today, some backend APIs return the stored alias. The frontend compensates for this in the MT mapper.

## Aliased datasource plugins

| Alias (stored type) | Canonical plugin ID |
| --- | --- |
| `postgres` | `grafana-postgresql-datasource` |
| `phlare` | `grafana-pyroscope-datasource` |
| `testdata` | `grafana-testdata-datasource` |

The `postgres` alias has the highest volume. Postgres datasources from before the rename keep the stored type `postgres`.

## Current behavior

The backend returns the stored alias in these locations:

| Surface | Value for a `postgres` row | Location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connections, service | `plugin: postgres`, `group: postgres.datasource.grafana.app` | `pkg/services/datasources/service/datasource.go` (`asConnection`) |
| Connections, legacy client | The same values, from `conn.Type` | `pkg/api/datasource/connections.go` (`GetConnectionByUID`) |
| Unified storage migration | Group label `postgres.datasource.grafana.app` | `pkg/registry/apis/datasource/migrator/migrator.go` |

Grafana registers each datasource API group with the canonical plugin ID only (`pkg/registry/apis/datasource/register.go`).
Thus, no server serves the group `postgres.datasource.grafana.app`.

These locations already handle aliases correctly:

- The legacy per-plugin list adds the alias types to its SQL query (`plugincontext.go`, `service/store.go`).
- The converter accepts alias types on read. It writes the canonical ID on create and update (`converter/converter.go`).
- The query client maps each alias to the canonical group (`pkg/registry/apis/query/client/plugin.go`).
- `pluginstore.CanonicalPluginID` and `pluginstore.SamePlugin` resolve aliases (#130100).
- `GET /api/datasources` and `GET /api/datasources/uid/:uid` normalize `type` to the canonical ID.
- Boot data normalizes `type` to the canonical ID.

The frontend compensates in `packages/grafana-runtime/src/services/dataSource/sources/mt/mappers.ts`:

- `toListSnapshot` matches plugin metadata on the plugin ID and on each alias.
- `getConnectionPluginType` reads the plugin type from the group string when `plugin` is empty.

## Suspected bug: unified storage label mismatch

The migrator labels each object with the group from the stored type.
A `postgres` row gets the label `postgres.datasource.grafana.app`.
A list request on `grafana-postgresql-datasource.datasource.grafana.app` selects on the canonical label.
Thus, the list does not return the migrated `postgres` rows.

We did not confirm this at runtime. The first task is an integration test that shows the behavior.

## Scope

In scope:

- The connections API: `query.grafana.app` connections and the legacy `ConnectionClient`.
- The per-plugin datasource resource: `<plugin>.datasource.grafana.app`, in legacy storage mode and in unified storage mode.

Out of scope:

- `GET /api/datasources` and boot data. These already normalize `type`. The per-type tweak fix below is the only exception.
- Writes through the legacy `POST /api/datasources`.

## Decisions

1. **Canonical values only.** API responses contain the canonical plugin ID and the canonical group. Responses do not show the stored alias.
2. **Read-time mapping first.** Phase 1 maps the stored type with `CanonicalPluginID` when it builds a response. Phase 1 does not change stored data.
3. **Writes store the canonical ID.** Create and update through the new APIs persist the canonical ID. This prevents new alias rows.
4. **Unified storage uses the canonical label on write.** The migrator and the write path set the canonical group label. Until the Phase 2 rewrite, the read path also selects the alias labels.
5. **Fix the per-type tweaks in both places.** Boot data and the MT mapper must match on the canonical ID.
6. **Provisioning maps aliases on the fly.** A provisioning file can use an alias, for example `type: postgres`. Provisioning must store the canonical ID. Users do not need to change their files.

## Provisioning

Datasource provisioning sends the `type` from the file to `AddDataSource` and `UpdateDataSource` without a change (`pkg/services/provisioning/datasources/datasources.go`).
Provisioning runs again at each startup. Thus, a file with `type: postgres` creates new alias rows. It also writes the alias back into rows that already have the canonical ID.
This breaks decision 3. It also reverses the Phase 2 rewrite at each startup.

Requirements:

- Provisioning resolves the file `type` with `CanonicalPluginID` before it creates or updates a datasource.
- Provisioning does not fail when the file uses an alias.
- Provisioning logs a deprecation warning when the file uses an alias. The warning shows the canonical ID.
- Correlation provisioning uses the canonical ID for `SourceType` and for the target type.
- If the plugin is not installed, provisioning cannot resolve the alias. Then provisioning stores the file `type` without a change. This is the current behavior.

## Work items

Phase 1: read-time mapping

- [ ] Add an integration test for the unified storage list. Use a migrated `postgres` row and list on the canonical group.
- [ ] Return the canonical `plugin` and `group` from `asConnection` in `service/datasource.go`.
- [ ] Return the canonical `plugin` and `group` from the legacy `GetConnectionByUID`.
- [ ] Set the canonical group label in the migrator.
- [ ] Set the canonical group label on unified storage writes.
- [ ] Make the unified storage list select the canonical label and each alias label.
- [ ] Make the per-plugin get by name return a row whose stored type is an alias. Do this in both storage modes.
- [ ] Confirm that create and update through the per-plugin API store the canonical ID.
- [ ] Add tests for each API with a row that stores an alias type.

Provisioning:

- [ ] Map the file `type` to the canonical ID in `createInsertCommand` and `createUpdateCommand`, or in the step before them.
- [ ] Log a deprecation warning for each datasource whose file `type` is an alias.
- [ ] Use the canonical ID in correlation provisioning.
- [ ] Confirm that the plugin store is ready before datasource provisioning starts. If the store is not ready, provisioning cannot resolve the alias.
- [ ] Add tests: a file with an alias type, a file with the canonical type, and a file whose plugin is not installed.

Per-type tweak fix (separate PRs for backend and frontend):

- [ ] Backend: in `getFSDataSources` (`pkg/api/bootdata.go`), match the per-type tweaks on the canonical ID. Today, `postgres` rows do not get the `database` fallback because `DS_POSTGRES` is `grafana-postgresql-datasource`.
- [ ] Frontend: in `applyPerTypeTweaks` (`mappers.ts`), match on the canonical ID. Update the comment that describes parity with boot data.

Frontend follow-up, after the backend changes ship:

- [ ] Remove the alias lookup from `toListSnapshot`, or keep it only as a fallback for older backends. The frontend and the backend deploy at different times.
- [ ] Decide if `getConnectionPluginType` still needs the group fallback.

Phase 2: rewrite stored data (TBD)

- [ ] Decide the scope before we write the migration. Possible parts:
  - The `type` column in the `data_source` table.
  - The group labels of objects that unified storage already stores.
  - Provisioning: the on-the-fly mapping above must ship before the rewrite. Otherwise, provisioning writes the alias again at the next startup.
  - Datasource references in dashboards and queries that use an alias.

## Open questions

1. **Datasources without an installed plugin.** What do the new APIs return for a datasource whose plugin is not installed?
   - Today, `GET /api/datasources` returns these datasources. It has no explicit field to show this. The signals are implicit: the generic logo, a `typeName` equal to the stored type, and a `type` that the API does not normalize.
   - Today, boot data omits these datasources and logs an error. The MT list does the same.
   - Option A: The connections API omits them and logs an error, like boot data.
   - Option B: The connections API returns them with an explicit flag, for example a label or a condition. A management UI can then show "plugin not installed".
   - The per-plugin resource cannot serve them, because Grafana does not register an API group for a plugin that is not installed.
2. **Backwards compatibility between services.** Unified storage can deploy at a different time than the API layer. Make sure that the label change and the read change work in both deploy orders. Refer to `pkg/storage/unified/AGENTS.md`.

## Query a Health Model as a node graph 

### Summary
Execute the Azure Monitor Health Models query type in the Go backend and return a node graph (nodes and edges), coloured by entity health state, at the end of the dashboard time range. Each node shows its health state. This follows the existing Resource Graph pattern in `pkg/tsdb/azuremonitor`: plain ARM REST calls through the data source's authenticated HTTP client. The feature flag controls discoverability only, so there is no flag check in the backend.

### In scope
- Add a `healthmodels` package in `pkg/tsdb/azuremonitor`, modelled on `resourcegraph/azure-resource-graph-datasource.go`. Register it in the query-type routing in `azuremonitor.go` alongside Metrics, Logs and Resource Graph.
- Call the ARM REST API directly (`http.NewRequestWithContext` plus the data source's HTTP client). Reuse the client built in `httpclient.go`, which signs requests via `azhttpclient.AddAzureAuthentication`, so every credential type keeps working. No `armcloudhealth` dependency.
- Once the `healthModelResourceId` is saved, fetch the latest Health Model with a GET on that resource ID (`getHealthModel`), before the entity and relationship calls. In future, this call will return the data plane URL used for entity health.
- Put the Health Model calls behind one small interface, `HealthModelClient` (`getHealthModel`, `listEntities` and `listRelationships`), with an ARM implementation (`armHealthModelClient`) for now. The handler depends only on the interface, so a data plane client can be added later as a separate implementation with its own authentication.
- Frame builders take plain structs (`HealthModel`, `Entity`, `Relationship`), not ARM response types.
- Use API version `v11`.
- Pin the entity and relationship requests to the end of the query time range with the `timestamp` parameter, fetch them in parallel, and follow `nextLink` paging.
- Validate that `healthModelResourceId` is a well-formed `Microsoft.CloudHealth/healthmodels` ID and that its subscription matches the query's subscription. Return a clear error otherwise.
- Apply template variable interpolation to `subscription` and `healthModelResourceId` before execution.
- Build the node graph data frames:
  - Nodes: id (entity name), title (display name), subtitle (health state) and colour from health state.
  - Node center: `mainstat` shows the health state text.
  - Edges: id, source and target from the relationship's parent and child entity names.
  - Set the preferred visualisation type to the node graph.
  - Key nodes by entity name, since display names aren't unique.
  - Drop edges that point to entities outside the model, so no stateless ghost nodes appear.
  - Use fixed health state colours (Healthy, Degraded, Unhealthy, Unknown), with unknown states falling back to the Unknown colour.
- Return per-query errors for auth, permission, not-found and throttling failures with actionable messages.
- Route Health Models queries to the backend in the frontend.
- Add unit tests for the get-model call, ID validation, template interpolation, paging, frame building, edge filtering, colour mapping and error mapping, using a fake `HealthModelClient`. Follow the existing test patterns for the Resource Graph handler.

### Out of scope
- A data plane client and its authentication (future work).
- Signal information, including the healthy signal count on nodes (future ticket).
- Alert severities and impact information on nodes.
- Entity history, time series output and the Format selector (ticket 3).
- A feature flag check in the backend.
- Alerting support.
- User documentation, which lands with ticket 3.

### Acceptance criteria
- A query with a subscription and model renders in the Node graph panel, with nodes coloured by health state and edges matching the model's relationships.
- Each node's center shows its health state.
- Entities with no relationships still appear as nodes.
- Relationships pointing at entities outside the model are not drawn.
- The latest Health Model is fetched before the entities, and a failure fetching it returns an actionable error.
- Model calls go through the `HealthModelClient` interface, and the handler has no direct dependency on ARM response types.
- Dashboard variables work in both subscription and model fields.
- A model that doesn't belong to the selected subscription returns a clear validation error.
- Models with more entities or relationships than one API page are fully loaded.
- Auth, permission, not-found and throttling failures show an actionable error message.
- Unit tests pass.

### Summary
Execute the Azure Monitor Health Models query type in the Go backend and return a node graph (nodes and edges), coloured by entity health state, at the end of the dashboard time range. Each node shows its health state. This follows the existing Resource Graph pattern in `pkg/tsdb/azuremonitor`: plain ARM REST calls through the data source's authenticated HTTP client. The feature flag controls discoverability only, so there is no flag check in the backend.

### In scope
- Add a `healthmodels` package in `pkg/tsdb/azuremonitor`, modelled on `resourcegraph/azure-resource-graph-datasource.go`. Register it in the query-type routing in `azuremonitor.go` alongside Metrics, Logs and Resource Graph.
- Call the ARM REST API directly (`http.NewRequestWithContext` plus the data source's HTTP client). Reuse the client built in `httpclient.go`, which signs requests via `azhttpclient.AddAzureAuthentication`, so every credential type keeps working. No `armcloudhealth` dependency.
- Once the `healthModelResourceId` is saved, fetch the latest Health Model with a GET on that resource ID (`getHealthModel`), before the entity and relationship calls. In future, this call will return the data plane URL used for entity health.
- Put the Health Model calls behind one small interface, `HealthModelClient` (`getHealthModel`, `listEntities` and `listRelationships`), with an ARM implementation (`armHealthModelClient`) for now. The handler depends only on the interface, so a data plane client can be added later as a separate implementation with its own authentication.
- Frame builders take plain structs (`HealthModel`, `Entity`, `Relationship`), not ARM response types.
- Use API version `v11`.
- Pin the entity and relationship requests to the end of the query time range with the `timestamp` parameter, fetch them in parallel, and follow `nextLink` paging.
- Validate that `healthModelResourceId` is a well-formed `Microsoft.CloudHealth/healthmodels` ID and that its subscription matches the query's subscription. Return a clear error otherwise.
- Apply template variable interpolation to `subscription` and `healthModelResourceId` before execution.
- Build the node graph data frames:
  - Nodes: id (entity name), title (display name), subtitle (health state) and colour from health state.
  - Node center: `mainstat` shows the health state text.
  - Edges: id, source and target from the relationship's parent and child entity names.
  - Set the preferred visualisation type to the node graph.
  - Key nodes by entity name, since display names aren't unique.
  - Drop edges that point to entities outside the model, so no stateless ghost nodes appear.
  - Use fixed health state colours (Healthy, Degraded, Unhealthy, Unknown), with unknown states falling back to the Unknown colour.
- Return per-query errors for auth, permission, not-found and throttling failures with actionable messages.
- Route Health Models queries to the backend in the frontend.
- Add unit tests for the get-model call, ID validation, template interpolation, paging, frame building, edge filtering, colour mapping and error mapping, using a fake `HealthModelClient`. Follow the existing test patterns for the Resource Graph handler.

### Out of scope
- A data plane client and its authentication (future work).
- Signal information, including the healthy signal count on nodes (future ticket).
- Alert severities and impact information on nodes.
- Entity history, time series output and the Format selector (ticket 3).
- A feature flag check in the backend.
- Alerting support.
- User documentation, which lands with ticket 3.

### Acceptance criteria
- A query with a subscription and model renders in the Node graph panel, with nodes coloured by health state and edges matching the model's relationships.
- Each node's center shows its health state.
- Entities with no relationships still appear as nodes.
- Relationships pointing at entities outside the model are not drawn.
- The latest Health Model is fetched before the entities, and a failure fetching it returns an actionable error.
- Model calls go through the `HealthModelClient` interface, and the handler has no direct dependency on ARM response types.
- Dashboard variables work in both subscription and model fields.
- A model that doesn't belong to the selected subscription returns a clear validation error.
- Models with more entities or relationships than one API page are fully loaded.
- Auth, permission, not-found and throttling failures show an actionable error message.
- Unit tests pass.

## Show Health Model entity history as a time series (backend and Format selector)

### Summary
Add a second result format that returns the health-state history of each entity over the dashboard time range. Add a **Format** selector to the editor to switch between the node graph and the history, and document the feature.

### In scope
- Add an optional `resultFormat` field to the query schema (`modelGraph` or `timeSeries`), defaulting to `modelGraph`, then regenerate the TS and Go types. Existing queries must keep returning the node graph.
- Add a **Format** selector to the Health Models editor, disabled until a model is selected.
- Add a `getEntityHistory` method to the `HealthModelClient` interface from ticket 2, with an ARM implementation that reuses the [ticket 2](https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/135377) request code, API version `v11` and error mapping:
  - POST `getHistory` per entity, with the dashboard start and end time.
  - Follow `nextMarker` paging, and fail if a marker repeats.
  - Fetch entities in bounded batches (for example 10 at a time) so large models don't flood the API.
- Build one stepwise series per entity:
  - Start at the range start with the entity's state before the first transition.
  - Add a point at each transition inside the range, sorted by time.
  - End at the range end with the entity's current state.
  - Map health states to stable enum values: `Healthy` is `0`, `Degraded` is `1`, `Unhealthy` is `2`, `Unknown` is `3`.
  - Use the display name and entity name for the series name, and fail clearly on an invalid timestamp.
- Switch the handler on `resultFormat`.
- Add user documentation for the Health Models editor, the formats and the permissions the data source identity needs.
- Add unit tests for the format switch, history paging, series building (including transitions on the range boundaries and an empty history), batching and error mapping.

### Out of scope
- Signal information, including the healthy signal count on nodes (future ticket).
- Alert severities and impact information.
- Alerting support.

### Acceptance criteria
- Selecting **Health Model Entity History** returns one series per entity, covering the full dashboard time range.
- Selecting **Health Model Graph**, or having no format saved, returns the node graph from ticket 2.
- The enum values are stable and match the documented mapping.
- Entities with more history than one page are fully loaded.
- A model with many entities completes without exceeding the batch limit.
- Documentation covers both formats and the required permissions.
- Unit tests pass.

body_text:
X-axis panning stops after a rerender that passes a new `queryZoom` callback with the same config.

Cause: the effect in `XAxisInteractionAreaPlugin.tsx` depends on `queryZoom`. A new callback runs the cleanup, which removes the pan listeners. The effect then registers an `init` hook that the existing plot never fires. Callers that pass an unstable callback lose panning after the first rerender. For example, `PanelRenderer` uses the default `onChangeTimeRange = () => {}`.

This bug existed before #132256.

Test: `XAxisInteractionAreaPlugin.test.tsx`, "pans through the latest queryZoom after the callback changes without a config change". When you fix the bug, change `it.failing` to `it`.

Related: https://github.com/grafana/grafana/pull/133401

body_text:
Restore the stable CodeMirror API after redesigning its export boundary. The original migration (grafana/grafana#134677, [DPRO-318](<https://linear.app/grafana/issue/DPRO-318/stabilize-and-expose-the-shared-codemirror-editor-api>)) was reverted in grafana/grafana#135327; exported runtime helpers can pull CM6 into the complete `@grafana/ui` namespace loaded by plugins.

* Keep runtime helpers such as `createCodeEditorTheme`, `signatureHelp`, and the variable-completion builders internal to the package. Construct their CM6 extensions behind the lazy editor boundary instead of adding another public helper entry point.
* Expose the customization existing consumers need through component props or callbacks. Start with transparent theme support; review signature-help providers and variable-completion configuration before settling the API.
* Restore stable editor, language metadata, and type exports, and update consumers and documentation. Preserve existing behavior, including notebooks, and the Monaco-backed root `CodeEditor`.
* Verify that initial app loading and plugin loading of the complete root UI namespace do not fetch CM6; the editor and requested languages should load on demand. Cover affected behavior with existing focused tests and inspect both profiled and unprofiled production Rspack builds.

body_text: **Why is this needed**: In a multi-value dashboard variable with "Include All option" enabled, selecting All only checks the "All" entry. Every individual value (e.g. FI, SE1, SE2, SE3, SE4) still shows an empty checkbox. This is confusing because: It looks like no individual values are included, even though all of them are. To exclude one value, users have to uncheck "All" and then check every other value one by one. Most users know filter dropdowns from Excel and similar tools, where "Select all" visibly checks every item. Current behavior in Grafana ("All" selected, but individual values unchecked): Expected behavior (example from Excel) ("Select All" checked, so every value is visibly checked): **What would you like to be added**: When All is selected, show every individual value as checked, like the Excel example above. Unchecking one value while "All" is active should deselect "All" and leave the remaining values checked, so it becomes an explicit multi-selection. Checking every individual value by hand should check "All" again (or show it as checked or partly checked). Optionally, show a partly checked state on "All" when only some values are selected. The variable's value should still work as it does today: when "All" is selected it should still resolve to $__all / the custom all value, so existing queries keep working. **Who is this feature for?** Dashboard users who work with multi-value variables that have the "All" option enabled.

**Why is this needed**:

I am a user of both the time-range copy-paste shortcuts (<kbd>t</kbd> <kbd>c</kbd>, <kbd>t</kbd> <kbd>v</kbd>) and the "recently used absolute time ranges" functionality.

When using <kbd>t</kbd> <kbd>v</kbd>, the time range is applied, but not appended to the "recently used" history.

**What would you like to be added**:

I would like that pasting a time range using <kbd>t</kbd> <kbd>v</kbd> would append that time range to the "recently used" history. (Same as clicking "apply time range".)

I'm happy to provide a PR if this is something people agree with.

**Who is this feature for?**

Dashboard users.

body_text:
### What happened?

When `[analytics] application_insights_connection_string` is set, Grafana loads the Application Insights JavaScript SDK and sends page views and interaction events. There are two problems.

**1. No user identity is sent**

`ApplicationInsightsBackend` gets only the connection string, the endpoint URL and the auto-route flag (`public/app/core/services/echo/init.ts`, `initAzureAppInsightsBackend`). It never calls `setAuthenticatedUserContext`. As a result:

- `user_Id` contains the random anonymous ID that the SDK stores in the `ai_user` cookie.
- `user_AuthenticatedId` is always empty.

You cannot connect telemetry to a Grafana user. One person who uses two browsers, or who clears cookies, counts as several users. The Rudderstack, PostHog and Faro backends do get `contextSrv.user`, but the Application Insights backend does not.

**2. `application_insights_auto_route_tracking` has no effect**

In `pkg/setting/setting.go`, the wrong key is read:

    cfg.ApplicationInsightsAutoRouteTracking = analytics.Key("application_insights_connection_string").MustBool(true)

The key should be `application_insights_auto_route_tracking` (the name in `conf/defaults.ini`). The connection string is not a boolean, so `MustBool(true)` always returns `true`. You cannot turn off auto-route tracking.

Because auto-route tracking is always on, and `addEvent` also calls `trackPageView()` for each Echo page view event, each route change probably sends two page views.

### What did you expect to happen?

1. Grafana calls `setAuthenticatedUserContext` with a stable, non-personal user identifier (for example `contextSrv.user.uid`) after `loadAppInsights()`. It keeps `user_Id` as the anonymous ID, as Microsoft recommends. Then `user_AuthenticatedId` contains the Grafana user UID.
2. `application_insights_auto_route_tracking = false` turns off the SDK auto-route tracking.

References:
- https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/app/data-model-complete#context
- https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/app/application-insights-faq
- https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/app/javascript-sdk-configuration

### Did this work before?

No. As far as I can tell, the Application Insights backend has never set an authenticated user context, and the configuration key bug is still on main.

### How do we reproduce it?

1. Set `[analytics] application_insights_connection_string = <connection string>` and `application_insights_auto_route_tracking = false`.
2. Sign in to Grafana and open some dashboards.
3. In Application Insights, run: `pageViews | where timestamp > ago(1h) | project timestamp, name, user_Id, user_AuthenticatedId, session_Id`
4. `user_Id` contains random values, `user_AuthenticatedId` is empty, and page views still arrive for each route change (auto-route tracking is still on).

### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

{"key": "grafana/grafana#135571", "repository": "grafana/grafana", "issue_number": 135571, "github_issue_id": "5960291412", "url": "https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/135571", "title": "Analytics: Application Insights backend sends no user identity, and application_insights_auto_route_tracking is ignored", "source_files": ["D:\OSS-Mentor\data\teacher_clickhouse\inventory_20261022T172108Z\issues_discovered.json"], "historical_labels": [], "beginner_difficulty_confirmed": false, "frozen": false, "decision": "availability_passed", "reason": "current_unassigned_no_observed_claim_or_open_pr", "open_pr_references": [], "claim_signals": [], "current_labels": ["type/bug", "area/backend", "area/configuration", "automated-triage"], "current_signal_group": "historical_signal_only", "body": "### What happened?

When `[analytics] application_insights_connection_string` is set, Grafana loads the Application Insights JavaScript SDK and sends page views and interaction events. There are two problems.

**1. No user identity is sent**

`ApplicationInsightsBackend` gets only the connection string, the endpoint URL and the auto-route flag (`public/app/core/services/echo/init.ts`, `initAzureAppInsightsBackend`). It never calls `setAuthenticatedUserContext`. As a result:

- `user_Id` contains the random anonymous ID that the SDK stores in the `ai_user` cookie.
- `user_AuthenticatedId` is always empty.

You cannot connect telemetry to a Grafana user. One person who uses two browsers, or who clears cookies, counts as several users. The Rudderstack, PostHog and Faro backends do get `contextSrv.user`, but the Application Insights backend does not.

**2. `application_insights_auto_route_tracking` has no effect**

In `pkg/setting/setting.go`, the wrong key is read:

    cfg.ApplicationInsightsAutoRouteTracking = analytics.Key("application_insights_connection_string").MustBool(true)

The key should be `application_insights_auto_route_tracking` (the name in `conf/defaults.ini`). The connection string is not a boolean, so `MustBool(true)` always returns `true`. You cannot turn off auto-route tracking.

Because auto-route tracking is always on, and `addEvent` also calls `trackPageView()` for each Echo page view event, each route change probably sends two page views.

### What did you expect to happen?

1. Grafana calls `setAuthenticatedUserContext` with a stable, non-personal user identifier (for example `contextSrv.user.uid`) after `loadAppInsights()`. It keeps `user_Id` as the anonymous ID, as Microsoft recommends. Then `user_AuthenticatedId` contains the Grafana user UID.
2. `application_insights_auto_route_tracking = false` turns off the SDK auto-route tracking.

References:
- https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/app/data-model-complete#context
- https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/app/application-insights-faq
- https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/app/javascript-sdk-configuration

### Did this work before?

No. As far as I can tell, the Application Insights backend has never set an authenticated user context, and the configuration key bug is still on main.

### How do we reproduce it?

1. Set `[analytics] application_insights_connection_string = <connection string>` and `application_insights_auto_route_tracking = false`.
2. Sign in to Grafana and open some dashboards.
3. In Application Insights, run: `pageViews | where timestamp > ago(1h) | project timestamp, name, user_Id, user_AuthenticatedId, session_Id`
4. `user_Id` contains random values, `user_AuthenticatedId` is empty, and page views still arrive for each route change (auto-route tracking is still on).

### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel?

N/A

### Environment (with versions)?

Grafana: 13.2.4 (Enterprise), official image grafana/grafana-enterprise:13.2.4 (also present on main)
OS: official Grafana container image, running on Azure Container Apps (Alpine Linux v3.24)
Browser: Safari 27.0.1

Kubernetes

body_text:
## Problem

The homepage shows errors when it calls APIs that are not yet available in multi-tenant (MT) mode. Examples include firing-alert requests and their teams/users dependencies.

The current test instance has an empty homepage. Connecting data sources introduces more requests to single-tenant endpoints, so handling only the initial empty state would leave gaps.

## Proposed work

- Audit homepage requests in MT mode, covering instances with and without connected data sources.
- Identify unsupported APIs and the homepage sections that depend on them, starting with alerts and teams/users lookups.
- Suppress non-critical error toasts for these known limitations.
- Hide affected optional sections or show a clear unavailable state. Avoid presenting unavailable data as a successful empty result or leaving sections loading indefinitely.
- Keep supported sections usable when another section’s request fails.
- Preserve actionable errors and existing single-tenant behavior.

body_text:
## Problem

Text panel v2 suggests `${__data.fields.*}` macros in Once mode, but they require a row context and remain unresolved.

#133744 describes this mismatch. #133951 proposes using the row containing the first non-time field’s last non-null value as context for all field macros.

That introduces implicit coupling: one field determines which row every other field reads. Standard field reductions operate independently, so different fields’ last non-null values can come from different rows.

## Proposal

Allow data macros to specify a reducer explicitly. Each referenced field is reduced independently across its values, without assigning a shared row context.

Illustrative syntax, subject to compatibility with existing macro parsing and variable formatting:

```text
Latest CPU: ${__data.fields.cpu:reduce:lastNotNull}
Average CPU: ${__data.fields.cpu:reduce:mean}
Peak memory: ${__data.fields.memory:reduce:max}
```

Reuse Grafana’s existing reducers and field display formatting. Autocomplete should help users discover supported reducers.

## Expected behavior

Given:

| Time | CPU | Memory |
|---|---:|---:|
| 10:00 | 40 | 100 |
| 10:01 | 75 | null |
| 10:02 | null | 120 |

Independent `lastNotNull` reductions return CPU = `75` and Memory = `120`, despite coming from different rows.

Reduction does not establish a source row for other macros. In particular, reducers such as mean and sum have no corresponding source timestamp. Reducing the Time field independently must not imply that its result is the timestamp of another field’s reduced value.

## Acceptance criteria

- Explicit reducer macros resolve in Once mode without a row context.
- Each field reduces independently using existing Grafana reducer semantics.
- Reduced values respect field display configuration, including units and decimals.
- Autocomplete offers supported reducers and avoids suggesting bare row-dependent macros where no row context exists.
- Existing Per row macros retain their behavior.
- Tests cover independent last-non-null values, aggregate reducers, null/empty inputs, and display formatting.

## Scope

Start with Text panel v2. Shared macro support can be evaluated during implementation. Selecting a common row or exposing the source timestamp of a reduced value is outside this proposal.

Related: #133744, #133951.

body_text: Labels for points of interest (POIs: shops, stations, parks) and cities are drawn on top of their own icons. This occurs in every Protomaps flavor at zoom 15 and higher. In the original Protomaps renderer, each label is beside its icon. The cause is in the style. The `pois`, `places_locality` and `places_region` layers set the label position with `text-variable-anchor: ["left","right"]` and `text-offset: [1.1, 0]`. ol-mapbox-style does not support `text-variable-anchor`. Thus each label uses the center anchor, and the offset moves it only a small distance. A possible fix is in `adaptStyle` in `public/app/plugins/panel/geomap/layers/basemaps/protomaps.ts`. When a layer has `text-variable-anchor`, set `text-anchor` to the first value of that list. To reproduce: 1. Set the `grafana.geomapProtomapsBasemap` feature flag to true. 2. Start a Protomaps tile server on `http://localhost:8095/`. 3. Open the `geomap-basemap-comparison` dev dashboard and go to the panels for Lower Manhattan at zoom 15. Found in the comparison for #135470.

body_text: At zoom 16 and 17, many POI (point of interest) labels and icons overlap each other in Protomaps. The text is difficult to read in Lower Manhattan. CARTO shows almost no POIs at the same zoom. This issue can have the same cause as the label position issue. OpenLayers calculates the collision box of each label from its position. A label in the wrong position thus gets the wrong collision box. Do the test again after the fix for the label position. If the overlap continues, reduce the number of POIs at these zoom levels. To reproduce, open the `geomap-basemap-comparison` dev dashboard with the `grafana.geomapProtomapsBasemap` feature flag set to true. Go to the row "Overzoom z17". Found in the comparison for #135470.

body_text: In the Protomaps dark flavor, the land has a dark green tint at zoom 1 to 4. Green markers are almost invisible on that land. The default color scheme of the panel (`GrYlRd`, green to yellow to red) starts with green, so most markers in a new panel are green. CARTO dark-matter uses black land, and the same markers are visible. The Protomaps black flavor does not have this problem. The decision on the default flavor in #135478 must include this result. Another possible fix is to remove the green land cover from the dark style at low zoom. Found in the comparison for #135470.

body_text: The Protomaps light flavor uses strong colors for water (cyan) and for land cover (green and tan). At zoom 1 to 4, these colors make data layers difficult to read. For example, a yellow heatmap is not clear over the tan desert, and a green GeoJSON layer is not clear over green land. The white and grayscale flavors show the same data clearly. CARTO positron also shows it clearly. This result is input for the default flavor in #135478. Data on top of the map is the main use of the geomap panel. Thus a muted flavor is a better default than the light flavor. To reproduce, open the `geomap-basemap-comparison` dev dashboard with the `grafana.geomapProtomapsBasemap` feature flag set to true. Go to the row "Data layers". Found in the comparison for #135470.

body_text: At zoom 4, Protomaps shows a label for each US state and for many cities. CARTO shows only the country name at the same zoom. The Protomaps labels do not collide, but the map is busier and data on top is more difficult to read. This issue occurs in the light and dark flavors. A possible fix is to remove the state labels and the smaller city labels below zoom 5 in `adaptStyle`. The "Show labels" option already removes all labels, but some users want to keep a few labels. Found in the comparison for #135470.

body_text: In the Protomaps dark flavor, city labels are dim gray at zoom 10. In CARTO dark-matter, the same labels are white and easy to read. The Protomaps labels have low contrast against the dark land. A possible fix is a lighter label color for the `places_locality` layer in the dark style. This issue is cosmetic. Found in the comparison for #135470.

body_text: ### What happened? A query variable's editor does not display its datasource or query configuration when the datasource is referenced through a datasource variable in the same dashboard row. Selecting the concrete Prometheus datasource directly: - Displays the selected datasource. - Displays the Prometheus query editor. - Returns the expected label values. Selecting the row-scoped datasource variable instead: - Displays "Select data source". - Hides the Prometheus query type and query configuration controls. When a valid query and the datasource variable reference are preserved in the dashboard JSON, running the query returns the expected values. However, the datasource selector still displays "Select data source", and the query editor remains hidden. The exact root cause has not been confirmed. ### What did you expect to happen? The editor should resolve the datasource selected by the datasource variable in the same row, retain the variable reference, and display the appropriate Prometheus query editor. Both variables should remain scoped to that row so that different rows can select their datasources independently. ### Did this work before? Unknown. Selecting the concrete datasource directly works in the same environment. Selecting it through a row-scoped datasource variable exhibits the issue. ### How do we reproduce it? Prerequisite: A configured Prometheus datasource containing at least one time series with a "cluster" label. The names below are illustrative. 1. Create a dashboard using dashboard.grafana.app/v2. 2. Add a row. 3. In that row, create a datasource variable: - Name: ROW_PROMETHEUS - Type: Prometheus - Select the configured Prometheus datasource - Multi-value: disabled - Include All: disabled 4. In the same row, create a query variable named Cluster. 5. Select the concrete Prometheus datasource directly. 6. Configure: - Query type: Label values - Label: cluster 7. Run the query and confirm that values are returned. 8. Change the target datasource to ${ROW_PROMETHEUS}. 9. Observe that "Select data source" is displayed and the Prometheus query configuration controls disappear. Additional observation: If the valid query and variable datasource reference are retained in dashboard JSON, query execution returns the expected values, but the datasource selector and query editor remain broken. ### Is the bug inside a dashboard panel? Screenshot 1: Selecting the concrete datasource displays the Prometheus query editor and returns label values. Screenshot 2: Selecting the row-scoped datasource variable displays "Select data source" and hides the query editor, while query results are still available with the query preserved in dashboard JSON. Internal identifiers have been redacted. ### Environment (with versions)? Grafana version: 13.2.4 Prometheus datasource plugin version: 13.2.3 (shown in plugin UI) Installation: RPM package + systemd Grafana server OS: Linux (exact distribution/version to be added) Browser: Safari (exact version to be added) Client OS: macOS (exact version to be added) Dashboard schema: dashboard.grafana.app/v2 No custom Grafana source patch has been applied. ### Grafana platform? None ### Datasource(s)? _No response_
